entries.title: Wounds
entries.summary: Damage beyond Soak becomes wounds; a character can have many wounds, their penalties add up and apply to all actions but not Soak, and non-fatal wounds cannot kill immediately.
quotes: The character suffers a penalty to all actions (rolls and totals) equal to the sum of all penalties due to his wounds

entries.title: Damage Table (Wounds)
entries.summary: Repeat of the Damage Table converting damage past Soak into wound levels by Size.
quotes: For every 5 + size points by which the Damage Total exceeds the Soak Total, the wound level increases by one.

entries.title: Wound Table
entries.summary: Table of the penalty each wound level applies to actions, with Incapacitated characters unable to act.
quotes: The character may not undertake any actions.

entries.title: Recovering From Wounds
entries.summary: Each wound gets a Recovery roll at an interval depending on its severity, compared with Stable and Improvement Ease Factors, so wounds may improve, hold steady with a bonus, or worsen.
quotes: RECOVERY TOTAL: Stamina + Medic's Chirurgy or Medicine score + Magical Aid + Stress Die
Recovery rolls do not suffer from the Wound Penalty.

entries.title: Chirurgy
entries.summary: Medieval surgery used to help others recover from physical damage; the rules for its use are on the wound recovery page.
quotes: See page 405 for rules.

entries.title: Activities While Injured
entries.summary: What a wounded character can safely do at each band of Wound Penalty, including travel, study and lab work, and the Recovery roll risked by overexertion.
quotes: Any character who does more than his injuries allow must make an immediate Recovery roll for his most serious wound.

entries.title: Recovery from Incapacitation
entries.summary: Incapacitated characters make two Recovery rolls a day, dying on a low result and improving to Heavy on a high one, with a cumulative penalty otherwise.
quotes: On a roll of 0 or less, the character dies.

entries.title: Medical Attention
entries.summary: A medic's Chirurgy (for injuries) or Medicine (for disease and poison) adds to Recovery rolls; only one Ability can help with a given wound.
quotes: Combat wounds and similar injuries require Chirurgy, while diseases and poison require Medicine.

entries.title: Recovery Modifiers
entries.summary: Table of cumulative modifiers for living conditions, diet, activity, missing instruments or herbs and self-treatment that apply to Chirurgy and Medicine rolls and to Wound and Disease Recovery rolls, with an extra botch die for each modifier that applies.
quotes: for each modifier that applies from this list the Chirurgy or Medicine roll receives one extra botch die

entries.title: Healing Spells
entries.summary: Creo Corpus rituals can heal wounds immediately, while other Creo Corpus spells add a bonus to Recovery rolls for as long as they remain in effect, and may cause Warping.
quotes: Certain Creo Corpus rituals can heal wounds immediately, without requiring a roll

related.text: ArM5 p.332 The Chirurgeon's Healing Touch

entries.title: Injuries (Non-Combat Damage)
entries.summary: Non-combat damage adds a damage bonus to a stress die and soak adds a stress die to Soak; the same rules calculate spell damage.
quotes: NON-COMBAT DAMAGE TOTAL: Damage Bonus + Stress Die
NON-COMBAT SOAK TOTAL: Soak Total + Stress Die.

entries.title: Heat and Corrosion
entries.summary: Damage bonus from heat and corrosion is multiplied by how much of the body is exposed and inflicted once per combat round.
quotes: If it covers an entire limb, the damage bonus is doubled.

entries.title: Heat and Corrosion Table
entries.summary: Table of intensity bonuses for common heat and corrosion sources.

entries.title: Impact
entries.summary: Damage from falling or falling objects is taken once, with a table of sample impact damage bonuses.
quotes: Characters may also take damage from falling, or having things fall on them.

entries.title: Injury and wound location
entries.summary: Injuries are treated with Chirurgy, with Medicine only helping against infection. Offers an optional way to determine the location and form of Medium, Heavy and Incapacitating wounds.
quotes: All injuries are treated using the Chirurgy Ability

entries.title: Optional Rule: Lasting Consequences of Serious Damage
entries.summary: Optional rule: when an Incapacitating wound is dealt the player rolls Stamina, and failure gives a lasting Minor Flaw complication, possibly leading to loss of a limb through surgery.
quotes: the player should immediately make a Stamina roll, against an Ease Factor of 6

entries.title: Crushing Damage
entries.summary: Examples of what injuries crushing damage causes at Medium, Heavy and Incapacitating or Fatal wound levels.

entries.title: Piercing Damage
entries.summary: Examples of what injuries piercing damage causes at Medium, Heavy and Incapacitating or Fatal wound levels.

entries.title: Slashing Damage
entries.summary: Examples of what injuries slashing damage causes at Medium, Heavy and Incapacitating or Fatal wound levels.

entries.title: Burns and Scalds
entries.summary: Examples of what injuries burns, scalds, cold and poison cause at Medium, Heavy and Incapacitating or Fatal wound levels.

entries.title: Battlefield Injuries (activity while wounded)
entries.summary: Describes how Wound Penalties restrict travel, strenuous activity, sentry duty and double watches, and why a first-aider's Chirurgy matters for the Wound Recovery roll that prevents a wound from worsening.
quotes: Even a –1 Wound Penalty prohibits strenuous activity without risking the wound.

entries.title: First Aid
entries.summary: A chirurgeon can make a First Aid roll against the Improvement Ease Factor of a patient's worst wound to treat him as one category higher for Activity While Injured for a day; a botch provokes an immediate Wound Recovery roll.
quotes: Dexterity + Chirurgy + Recovery Modifiers (see Art & Academe, page 54) + Magical Aid + stress die vs Improvement Ease Factor

entries.title: Magical First Aid
entries.summary: Hermetic spells and enchantments that prevent wounds from worsening or help recovery, including Bind Wound, low-level Creo Corpus bonuses to Wound Recovery, Endurance of the Berserkers, and a Sun-duration Chirurgeon's Healing Touch that causes Warping.
quotes: prevents any wound from worsening while in effect

entries.title: Combat Scores
entries.summary: The five combat scores (Initiative, Attack, Defense, Damage, Soak) and the formulas for each total, plus Attack Advantage.
quotes: ATTACK TOTAL: Dexterity + Combat Ability + Weapon Attack Modifier + Stress Die
DEFENSE TOTAL: Quickness + Combat Ability + Weapon Defense Modifier + Stress Die
ATTACK ADVANTAGE: Attacker's Attack Total - Defender's Defense Total

entries.title: Combat Botches
entries.summary: Sidebar on how botched combat rolls reduce the total to zero (and why a botched Defense is so deadly), with an exception for combatants with a negative base Defense.
quotes: A botch on a combat roll reduces the total to zero, just as for any other botch.

entries.title: Combat Sequence
entries.summary: Step-by-step combat round: one Initiative roll for the whole fight, parties act in decreasing order, attacker and defender each roll a stress die, and a hit deals damage minus Soak.
quotes: Initiative is determined once for the whole combat, and then remains the same every round.
If you miss, you cannot do any damage, no matter how high your Damage Total.

entries.title: Length of a Combat Round
entries.summary: A combat round lasts about six seconds, which also determines how many rounds a Diameter spell lasts.
quotes: A combat round lasts for about six seconds, so that a Diameter Duration spell lasts for twenty rounds.

entries.title: Damage Table
entries.summary: Table converting damage past Soak into a wound level (Light to Dead) for each creature Size, with the rule for extrapolating beyond the table.
quotes: For every 5 + size points by which the Damage Total exceeds the Soak Total, the wound level increases by one.

entries.title: Initiative Ties
entries.summary: Worked example of re-rolling tied Initiative, where the re-roll only orders the tied parties relative to each other.
quotes: The reroll only determines the relative ordering of C, D, and E; it does not over-ride the initial initiative result.

entries.title: Spell Damage
entries.summary: Sidebar explaining how a spell's listed damage is turned into a Damage Total with a stress die and how Soak is applied, and that Attack Advantage does not change spell damage.
quotes: The target's Soak Total + Stress Die is then subtracted from this to determine the wounds suffered.

entries.title: Combat: Simple Example
entries.summary: Worked example of two-party combat showing Initiative, Attack, Defense, botch checks, Attack Advantage, Soak, the Damage Table and Wound Penalties across two rounds.

entries.title: Missile Combat
entries.summary: Range increment penalties for missile attacks and the rule that only a shield's Defense bonus helps against missiles.
quotes: The Attack Total suffers a -3 penalty for every range increment beyond the first between the attackers and the defenders.

entries.title: Moving in Combat
entries.summary: Three movement speeds in combat (walk, hurry, run) with pace-per-round formulas, and the length of a pace.
quotes: WALK: 10 + Qik – Encumbrance paces per round
HURRY: 2 x (10 + Qik – Encumbrance) paces per round
RUN: 4 x (10 + Qik – Encumbrance) paces per round

entries.title: Fatigue Levels
entries.summary: Names the Fatigue levels from Fresh to Unconscious, explains that Short-Term and Long-Term losses share one track, and gives the penalties that apply to rolls other than Soak.
quotes: Most characters have six Fatigue levels
The penalty for Weary is -1, for Tired -3, and for Dazed -5.

entries.title: Short-Term Fatigue
entries.summary: Strenuous actions require a Fatigue roll on Stamina minus Encumbrance against an Ease Factor; failure costs a Short-Term Fatigue level and a botch costs two, with combat and magic using their own rules.
quotes: roll Stamina — Encumbrance on a stress die against an Ease Factor of 6

entries.title: Recovery from Short-Term Fatigue
entries.summary: Fatigue is recovered one level at a time with rest, using the Fatigue Recovery Chart, with an optional Stamina roll to halve the time.
quotes: Success allows recovery in half the normal time.

entries.title: Long-Term Fatigue
entries.summary: Extended exertion costs Long-Term Fatigue levels at the storyguide's discretion, regained only by a good night's rest, with the more serious levels treated as short term.
quotes: One night's rest removes one Long-Term Fatigue level.

entries.title: Fatigue Recovery Chart
entries.summary: Table of the time needed to recover from each Fatigue level to the next lower one.

entries.title: Botches
entries.summary: A botched casting gives a Casting Total of zero but the spell still goes wrong in a harmful way, scaled by the number of zeros on the botch dice, and each zero gives a Warping Point, risking Twilight.
quotes: Magi gain one Warping Point for every zero that comes up on the botch dice when casting a spell.

entries.title: Sources of Botch Dice
entries.summary: Lists standard modifiers to the number of botch dice when casting (vis, supernatural auras, fast casting, familiar Golden Cord, spell mastery) and when a relaxed Formulaic caster has none.
quotes: Using vis while casting: +1 botch die per pawn of vis used
Casting in a supernatural aura other than Magic: +1 botch die per level of the aura, doubled if in a regio
Golden Cord to a familiar: -1 botch die per level

entries.title: Botch Suggestions
entries.summary: A list of suggested botch results (unwanted attention, caster addled or overwhelmed, reverse effect, wrong target, undying spell and so on) for the storyguide to adapt.
quotes: Caster overwhelmed: You are overwhelmed by your own magic. Make a Stamina stress roll of 6+ or be knocked unconscious.

entries.title: Brawl and Dodging
entries.summary: Brawl covers unarmed and improvised-weapon fighting and is the Ability used to dodge when a character has no Martial Abilities.
quotes: Brawl is also the Ability used to dodge attacks if you have no Martial Abilities.

entries.title: Disengaging
entries.summary: A party disengages by beating the Attack Totals of those who attacked it with a Defense Total, gaining a cumulative bonus on repeated attempts.
quotes: A party that tries to disengage repeatedly gets a +3 cumulative bonus for every attempt after the first

entries.title: Exertion
entries.summary: Spend a Fatigue level to add Combat Ability to an attack or to defense rolls for a round; groups must all spend a level and use the vanguard's Combat Ability.
quotes: By expending a Fatigue level you can add a bonus equal to your Combat Ability to either attack or defense for one round.

entries.title: Magic in Combat
entries.summary: Magi cast at their Quickness-based place in the initiative order, take about a round to cast, and may fast-cast in response to other actions.
quotes: A magus Fast Casting a spell (see page 217) acts in immediate response to another action, and thus not at a particular initiative point.

entries.title: Mounted Combat
entries.summary: A mounted fighter adds Ride, to a limit, to Attack and Defense Totals.
quotes: A mounted character adds his Ride score, to a maximum of +3, to his Attack and Defense Totals

entries.title: Non-Lethal Combat (Scuffling and Grappling)
entries.summary: Scuffles convert wound levels into lost Short-Term Fatigue, and grapples use Attack Advantage to build a Grapple Strength that the grappled character must reduce to escape.
quotes: A character attempting to grapple another succeeds if his Attack Advantage is greater than zero.
Fatigue levels inflicted in a scuffle are Short-Term Fatigue levels.

entries.title: Scuffle Effects
entries.summary: Table converting the wound level an attack would normally cause into Fatigue levels and lesser wounds in a scuffle.

entries.title: Special Combat Effects (Maneuvers)
entries.summary: Non-damaging maneuvers such as tripping or disarming use the normal combat sequence with a target Attack Advantage required to succeed, usually based on Brawl.
quotes: Follow the normal combat sequence, and set an Attack Advantage needed to succeed.

entries.title: Sample Advantages for Maneuvers
entries.summary: Table of required Attack Advantage for disarming, tripping, grabbing a worn item and taking a weapon.

entries.title: Chapter Nine: Optional Combat Rules
entries.summary: Introduces a chapter of optional, more detailed combat rules (tactical movement, mounted combat and more) that a troupe can adopt or ignore to keep combat simple.

entries.title: The Combat Round
entries.summary: Recaps the combat round (one action per character per round in Initiative order) and introduces the formal action categories used by the rest of the chapter, which may be ignored if the troupe prefers simple combat.
quotes: Each round represents about six seconds of time in the game world.

entries.title: When to Use Combat Rounds
entries.summary: Advises using the round-by-round structure for non-combat scenes such as chases, certamen or a courtly dance whenever the order of actions could affect the outcome.
quotes: A chase scene, a certamen, or even a complicated courtly dance could all be resolved by dividing the action into rounds

entries.title: Initiative
entries.summary: States when the storyguide calls for Initiative rolls and that any action not using a weapon, including spellcasting, has a weapon initiative modifier of zero.
quotes: Any action that doesn't require a weapon, including spellcasting, has a weapon initiative modifier of 0.

entries.title: When to Roll Initiative
entries.summary: Everyone present rolls Initiative when combat begins, while newcomers join the sequence only once they are within missile range or one round's movement of the fight.
quotes: Even characters who don't want to get involved in the battle should roll Initiative and act only on their turn.

entries.title: Actions in Combat
entries.summary: Defines an action as something a character can reasonably do in about one round on his own turn, including attacking and casting spells; a character normally performs one action per turn.
quotes: Normally, a character can perform one action on his turn.

entries.title: Not Everything is an Action
entries.summary: Rolls the storyguide demands, rather than ones the player initiates, are not actions, so a player can make any number of such rolls in a round.
quotes: There is no limit to how many die rolls a player can make in one round, because die rolls are not necessarily actions.

entries.title: Examples of Actions
entries.summary: A reference list of common actions such as attacking, casting, moving, charging, mounting and opening doors.
quotes: Mount or dismount a horse

entries.title: Reactions
entries.summary: Immediate responses to external events, such as Defense rolls, Fast Casting and Concentration rolls, are reactions that do not use up the character's action and have no per-round limit.
quotes: Reactions aren't actions, so they don't count against the limit of one action per round.

entries.title: Extended Actions
entries.summary: Rules for tasks that take a full round or longer: they cannot be delayed, exclude other actions while in progress, and need a Concentration roll if the character is distracted or attacked.
quotes: A character can't perform any other actions, including fast actions, while he is carrying out an extended action.

entries.title: Option: Fast Actions
entries.summary: Optional rule for brief activities like drawing a weapon or shouting a warning: a character can usually add one fast action to his regular action, or instead take several fast actions.
quotes: a character can perform one fast action, in addition to his regular action, on his turn
Alternatively, a character can perform up to four fast actions on his turn instead of any regular actions.

entries.title: Delaying Actions
entries.summary: A character may hold his action and use it later, responding only after an opponent's action finishes; where several characters delay, the highest Initiative Total responds first.
quotes: the delaying character with the highest Initiative Total has the first option to respond to a given event

entries.title: Option: Interrupting Actions
entries.summary: Optional rule letting a character who delayed his action interrupt an opponent through an action priority contest in which the winner resolves first; magi use Finesse and may still try Fast Casting afterwards.
quotes: Action Priority Total: Quickness + Ability – Encumbrance + stress die
Whoever has the highest Action Priority Total resolves his action first.

entries.title: Option: Fast Casting as Interruption
entries.summary: Variant replacing the Fast Casting speed roll's Ease Factor with the interrupted opponent's Action Priority Total, so Fast Casting and interrupting work alike.
quotes: use the interrupted opponent's Action Priority Total as the Ease Factor of the Fast Casting speed roll

entries.title: Tactical Movement
entries.summary: Introduces optional rules for handling movement on the battlefield in as much or as little detail as the troupe wants.

entries.title: Moving in Combat
entries.summary: Moving is an action with a choice of walk, hurry or run rates, each computed in paces per round from Quickness and Encumbrance; engaged characters must disengage first and running may require a Fatigue roll.
quotes: Walk: 10 + Quickness − Encumbrance paces per round
Hurry: 2 x (10 + Quickness – Encumbrance) paces per round
Run: 4 x (10 + Quickness – Encumbrance) paces per round

entries.title: Movement and Groups
entries.summary: Groups move as one unit at the speed of the slowest member, using the vanguard's Characteristics and Abilities for movement rolls.
quotes: Their speed is that of the slowest member.

entries.title: Obstacles, Barriers, and Movement
entries.summary: Difficult terrain halves movement speed and adds a botch die to Attack, Defense and movement rolls, and groups must make a Discipline check to cross it under the advanced group rules.
quotes: all difficult terrain slows movement to one-half normal speed

entries.title: Terrain Examples
entries.summary: Lists example difficult terrain, hazards and obstacles with their effects on movement and stress rolls, plus a small table of Ease Factors for forcing doors and picking locks; hazards add botch dice without slowing movement, obstacles need a specific effort to cross, and cover protects against missiles.
quotes: Movement speed halved (round up), extra botch die.
Extra botch die (or dice), botch potentially more serious.
Requires special action to move across.

entries.title: Engaging and Disengaging
entries.summary: Restates the two core engagement rules (a character is engaged when an enemy can plausibly attack him, and must disengage to move away) and says the following details are optional elaborations.
quotes: Once engaged, the character must disengage in order to move away from his opponent.

entries.title: Engaging in Combat
entries.summary: Explains when a character becomes engaged in melee or in missile combat, by making Attack or Defense rolls or by coming within reach or range of an enemy, and treats engagement as an abstraction represented by the disengagement roll.
quotes: A character becomes engaged in melee whenever he makes an Attack or Defense roll in melee combat.

entries.title: Effects of Being Engaged
entries.summary: An engaged character cannot move away from melee without disengaging; in missile combat he can move but must disengage to reach a location with better cover. A failed attempt stops movement for the round.
quotes: When a character who's engaged tries to disengage and fails, then the character's movement stops for the round and he remains engaged with his current opponent(s).

entries.title: Engagement and Defenders
entries.summary: Clarifies that under the standard defender rule defenders are always effective regardless of engagement, and points to the interceptor option as an alternative requiring an opposed roll.
quotes: an opponent cannot attack the character being protected as long as any of his defenders can lift a sword

entries.title: Option: No Engagement for Missile Combat
entries.summary: Optional rule that applies engagement and disengagement only to melee combat rather than to both melee and missile combat.
quotes: As an optional rule, you may use the engagement rules for melee combat only.

entries.title: Option: No Missiles While Engaged in Melee
entries.summary: Optional rule that forbids characters engaged in melee from making missile attacks.
quotes: As an optional rule, you may disallow characters engaged in melee from making missile attacks.

entries.title: Option: Defenders as Interceptors
entries.summary: A more complex alternative to the standard defender rule: the defender takes an extended action to guard a person or place and uses interrupting-action priority rolls to intercept melee and missile attackers, forcing them to target him instead. Includes a worked example.
quotes: A defender can only protect one other character, and only as long as that character remains within two paces of him.

entries.title: Attempting to Disengage
entries.summary: Disengaging is a reaction in which the mover's Defense Total must equal or beat the highest Attack Total of opponents who attacked him; repeated failed attempts earn a cumulative Defense bonus, and moving past an opponent with a delayed action lets that opponent attack.
quotes: If the character's Defense Total is greater than or equal to the highest Attack Total, the character may move normally.
he gains a +3 bonus to his Defense Total for his roll to disengage only

entries.title: Automatic Disengagement
entries.summary: Lists the circumstances in which a character is no longer engaged without needing a roll, such as all opponents being disabled or no one having attacked him since his last turn, and the extra missile-combat cases.
quotes: No opponents have attacked him since his last turn.

entries.title: Option: Reckless Disengagement
entries.summary: Optional rule allowing a character to simply move away from an opponent, at the cost of giving that opponent a free attack against a Defense Total of zero.
quotes: the character's opponent gets a free attack and the character gets no Defense roll: his Defense Total is 0

entries.title: Charging on Foot
entries.summary: A charge lets a character move and make a melee or thrown attack in the same round, costing a Fatigue level and granting an Attack bonus from his Combat Ability, but no Defense penalty; the bonus is lost on difficult terrain.
quotes: On foot, a charging character gains a bonus to his melee Attack roll equal to his Combat Ability.

entries.title: Option: Condensed Notation for Combat Scores
entries.summary: A character-sheet convention for recording a weapon's Defense with and without a shield as two numbers separated by a slash, so combat scores need not be recalculated if a shield breaks.
quotes: Axe/Heater Shield: Init +0, Attack +12, Defense +9/+11, Damage +7

entries.title: Option: Interrupting a Charge
entries.summary: Explains which Abilities enter the action priority contest when interrupting a charging character, and how to interrupt a charge by delaying and attacking if interrupting actions are not in use.
quotes: a character who is charging on foot uses his Combat Ability as the relevant Ability in his Action Priority Total

entries.title: Option: Ready Missiles
entries.summary: Used with the fast actions option: a bow or crossbow with a missile already on the string can be shot as a fast action, allowing a second action in the same round, with notes on how archers and crossbowmen reload.
quotes: He can shoot as a fast action instead of an ordinary action.

entries.title: Option: Constriction Attacks
entries.summary: Lets large creatures constrict a smaller victim using the grappling rules with fixed weapon statistics; a held victim is treated as deprived of air and makes periodic Stamina checks.
quotes: a constriction attack has the following weapon statistics: Initiative 0, Attack +3, Defense 0, Damage n/a

entries.title: Defending
entries.summary: Generating a Defense Total is a reaction, not an action, so a character can make any number of Defense rolls in a round and nearly always gets one even if he does not see the attack coming.
quotes: There is no limit to the number of Defense rolls a player may make for his character in one round.

entries.title: Defense when Unarmed
entries.summary: Unarmed characters defend with Brawl, while characters with only a shield defend using Single Weapon.
quotes: Completely unarmed characters use the Defense Total based on their Brawl Ability.

entries.title: Helpless Characters
entries.summary: A totally helpless character gets no Defense roll; his Defense Total is a fixed negative value.
quotes: treat his Defense Total as –10

entries.title: Option: Diceless Defense
entries.summary: Optional rule that replaces the stress die in Defense Totals with a constant, making Defense an Ease Factor for the Attack roll; it removes Defense botches and favors strong fighters, and can be applied selectively.
quotes: you can replace the stress die in characters' Defense Totals with a constant value of 6

entries.title: Option: No Defense for Missile Weapons
entries.summary: Optional rule that stops missile weapon Abilities from being used to generate a Defense Total: characters holding such weapons defend with Brawl, while javelins and throwing axes use Single Weapon.
quotes: A character holding a bow, crossbow, sling, knife, or stone uses the Brawl Ability for defense.

entries.title: Option: Evasion
entries.summary: Optional rule that splits dodging from blocking: Defense then applies only to melee attacks and Evasion, which depends on Size and Encumbrance, can be used against any attack. Gives separate on-foot and mounted Evasion Totals and can be combined with diceless defense.
quotes: Evasion Total on Foot: Quickness + Brawl − Size − Encumbrance + Shield Defense Modifier + stress die
Evasion Total While Mounted: Quickness + Ride − Size − Encumbrance + Shield Defense Modifier + stress die

entries.title: Option: Lasting Consequences of Serious Damage
entries.summary: Optional rule in which an Incapacitating Wound prompts a Stamina roll, and a failure leaves a lasting complication in the form of a Minor Flaw such as a lost limb.
quotes: the player should immediately make a Stamina roll against an Ease Factor of 6

entries.title: Option: Mitigating Deadly Wounds
entries.summary: Optional storyguide tool for trading a Major Wound for a lesser wound plus a permanent Flaw, with a rule of thumb for the trade and a list of suitable Minor and Major Flaws.
quotes: an Incapacitating Wound can be reduced to a Heavy Wound plus a Minor Flaw

related.text: Houses of Hermes: Mystery Cults p.136 Hobbled

entries.title: Mounted Combat
entries.summary: Lists the benefits of fighting from horseback: a situational Defense and melee Attack bonus tied to Ride, a separate action for the steed, proper use of the lance, special charge benefits and the ability to perform extended actions while the horse moves.
quotes: A mounted character gains a situational bonus to both Defense and melee Attacks equal to his Ride skill or +3,whichever is less.

entries.title: Suggestions for Combat Botches
entries.summary: A list of suggested botch results for combat rolls, ordered roughly from mild to severe, such as stumbling, dropping a weapon, colliding with an ally or a horse falling.
quotes: Stumble; −3 to Defense rolls until your next turn.

entries.title: Untrained Mounts
entries.summary: A rider on a horse not trained for battle gets no mounted-combat bonus, and the horse automatically panics when engaged in melee.
quotes: An untrained horse automatically panics whenever it is engaged in melee.

entries.title: Mounted Movement
entries.summary: A horse has four gaits and can use any of them in any round without building up speed.
quotes: A horse has four gaits, which are listed on the Mounted Movement Rates table.

entries.title: Charging on Horseback
entries.summary: A mounted charge combines movement and attack, adds the rider's Combat Ability to the Attack roll on top of the mounted bonus, and costs the horse rather than the rider a Fatigue level; the rider cannot also exert, and difficult terrain removes the bonus.
quotes: it is the horse, not the rider, who expends a Fatigue level

entries.title: Mounted Movement Rates
entries.summary: Tables of horse movement per round by gait and Quickness-type modifier, and of each gait's effects on missile Attack penalties, falling damage, the Ease Factor for extended actions in the saddle and an optional Defense bonus.
quotes: A horse must make a Fatigue test every round it moves at a gallop.

entries.title: Option: Shock of the Charge
entries.summary: Optional rule in which a mounted charge that hits a target smaller than the horse may knock it prone unless the target wins a reaction roll to stay upright.
quotes: Resist Charge While Mounted: Dexterity + Ride + saddle modifier + stress die vs. Damage Total (before Soak) + Size of attacker's horse
Resist Charge While on Foot: Str + Size + Combat Ability + stress die vs. Damage Total (before Soak) + Size of attacker's horse

entries.title: Shooting Missiles from Horseback
entries.summary: Mounted missile attacks take an Attack penalty that grows with the horse's gait, although a rider can move and shoot in the same round; the mounted Defense bonus applies but the mounted Attack bonus does not.
quotes: The Attack bonus for mounted combat does not apply to missile attacks.

entries.title: Actions Taken by Horses
entries.summary: A trained warhorse acts on its rider's turn and gets one action per turn (move or attack, not both), acts independently once the rider is unseated, and may use Confidence Points as directed by the rider's player.
quotes: The horse does not roll Initiative on its own; it acts on the rider's turn.

entries.title: Wounding Horses
entries.summary: Describes how a horse's wounds affect its rider by severity, from no effect for a Light Wound to Presence + Ride and Dexterity + Ride rolls for Medium and Heavy Wounds and a fall for the worst wounds.
quotes: the rider must make a Presence + Ride roll vs. Ease Factor 9 to control it

entries.title: Controlling a Panicked Horse
entries.summary: Sets when horses panic and the Presence + Ride roll needed to keep or regain control, with a reaction roll first and further attempts as actions; a panicked rider can do little else except complete a charge already begun.
quotes: Maintain or Regain Control of Panicked Horse: Presence + Ride vs. Ease Factor 6 – horse's total Wound Penalties

entries.title: Option: Defensive Bonus for Moving Horses
entries.summary: Optional rule that makes moving horses harder to hit with missiles, adding the gait-based bonus to Evasion if that option is used or otherwise to Defense against missile attacks.
quotes: The Mounted Movement Rates table lists an optional defensive bonus based on the horse's gait.

entries.title: Mounting and Dismounting
entries.summary: Mounting or dismounting in the usual way is an action that needs no die roll.
quotes: Mounting or dismounting a horse in the usual way is an action, but does not require a die roll.

entries.title: Leaping from the Saddle
entries.summary: A reaction roll lets a rider escape a panicking, falling or dying horse by leaping clear; with fast actions it can also be done voluntarily, and failure means falling.
quotes: Leap from the Saddle: Dexterity + Athletics – Encumbrance + stress die vs. Ease Factor 9

entries.title: Option: Vaulting Into the Saddle
entries.summary: With the fast actions option, a character can vault into the saddle as a fast action with a Strength + Athletics roll and may then ride in the same round if he did not move first.
quotes: Vault Into the Saddle: Strength + Athletics – Encumbrance + stress die vs. Ease Factor 6

entries.title: Falling from Horseback
entries.summary: A rider who falls takes falling damage that depends on the horse's gait, lands prone and must spend an action to stand up.
quotes: Any time a rider falls from his horse, he lands prone.

entries.title: Being Pinned Under a Horse
entries.summary: When a horse goes down, the rider may leap clear; otherwise he takes falling damage and rolls Quickness + Ride to avoid being crushed and pinned, requiring a Strength roll by another character to pull him out.
quotes: the horse lands on the rider, inflicting stress die + horse's Size + 6 damage

entries.title: Option: Non-Lethal Combat
entries.summary: Introduces an optional replacement for the standard non-lethal combat rules, with more varied maneuvers and with unarmed attacks causing Bruises rather than Fatigue loss.
quotes: unarmed attacks (scuffling) no longer cause Fatigue loss

entries.title: Non-Lethal Damage: Bruises
entries.summary: Non-lethal attacks inflict Bruises, which work like lesser wounds with Bruise Penalties but heal faster; damage is calculated as usual and the target suffers a Bruise of the same severity as the wound it would have been.
quotes: Calculate Damage from a non-lethal attack as usual, by subtracting the target's Soak score from the Damage Total.

entries.title: Recovering from Bruises
entries.summary: After resting for the Recovery Period a character rolls a Recovery Total for each Bruise; success improves it a category, serious Bruises leave one residual wound, and Ritual healing treats a Bruise as equivalent to its residual wound.
quotes: Recovery Total: Stamina + Medic's Medicine or Chirurgy score + magical aid + stress die

entries.title: Bruise Table
entries.summary: Table of Bruise levels giving each level's penalty, recovery interval, Improvement Ease Factor and the residual wound it leaves behind.
quotes: | Heavy | –5 | Two Hours | 15 | Light Wound |

entries.title: Your Arms are Too Short to Box with that Giant
entries.summary: Rule of thumb for scuffling, grappling and disarming against very large creatures: the giant gets a Defense bonus based on the Size difference against such attacks, but not against ordinary weapon attacks.
quotes: a giant gains a special bonus equal to double the difference between its Size and a smaller opponent's Size

entries.title: Weapons and Bruises
entries.summary: Weapons can be used to inflict Bruises at an Attack penalty; optionally clubs and similar weapons, and practice or tournament weapons, deal Bruises without that penalty.
quotes: suffer a −3 penalty to their Attack Total when they do so

entries.title: Special Effects
entries.summary: Rules for special maneuvers such as trips, grapples, pins, tackles, disarms and unseating riders, resolved by an Attack roll against a reaction with a required Attack Advantage, plus the effects of each maneuver and a table of example maneuvers.
quotes: Each maneuver requires a certain Attack Advantage in order to succeed.
The grappled defender suffers a –6 penalty on all attacks and most reactions, including Defense and Evasion, and can't perform spellcasting gestures.

entries.title: Example Maneuvers Table
entries.summary: Table listing each example maneuver with its Attack Total, the defender's choice of reaction and the Attack Advantage required.
quotes: | Disarm | Any Attack | Defense or Evasion | 9 |

entries.title: Fighting Invisibly
entries.summary: Rules for what invisibility does in a fight: protection from melee, missiles and targeted spells, Stealth bonuses, surprise attacks, and the limits of invisible weapons.
quotes: During the first round only, the invisible character automatically goes first and gains a +3 Attack bonus

entries.title: Locating an Invisible Character
entries.summary: Opposed roll procedure to pinpoint an invisible character well enough to attack or target him, and when location is automatic or needs no roll.
quotes: make an opposed Perception + Awareness roll against the invisible character's Dexterity + Stealth – Encumbrance + Stealth bonus

entries.title: Effects of Invisibility
entries.summary: Table giving melee Attack, Defense and Stealth bonuses for an invisible character according to how clear the visual signs of presence are.
quotes: Invisibility grants a bonus to melee attack rolls, but not to missile attacks.

entries.title: Invisibility and Group Combat
entries.summary: Invisible characters cannot fight as trained groups; an untrained group with invisible members gains extra botch dice.
quotes: everyone in the group gains an extra botch die per invisible character

entries.title: Armor
entries.summary: Armor is described by its material and by how much of the body it covers, and its Protection adds to Soak.
quotes: Two factors describe the armor a given character wears: what it is made of and how much of it the character is wearing.

entries.title: Armor Outfittings
entries.summary: Describes partial versus full armor and states that only the predominant material of a suit affects game statistics.
quotes: For simplicity, only the predominant material of the suit has any effect on game statistics (Protection and Load).

entries.title: Armor Table
entries.summary: Table of Protection, Load and Cost for partial and full armor of each material.
quotes: The bonus the armor grants to the character's Soak score.

entries.title: Melee Weapon Statistics
entries.summary: Table of Initiative, Attack, Defense and Damage modifiers, strength minimums, Load and Cost for brawling, single, and great melee weapons and shields.
quotes: The minimum strength requirements for a weapon and a shield must be met separately.

entries.title: Missile Weapon Statistics
entries.summary: Table of thrown and bow weapons with modifiers, range increments, strength minimums, Load and Cost.
quotes: The range increment for the weapon, in paces.

entries.title: Weapon Descriptions
entries.summary: Brief definitions of each weapon in the tables, including notes on how some are used (a lance only mounted, throwing weapons also usable in melee).
quotes: The lance may only be used from horseback, where it is a Single weapon.

entries.title: Crossbow Rules and Statistics
entries.summary: Interim rules for reloading crossbows (time depends on Strength and the winding system), a limit of one bolt per round, and a statistics table for historical and anachronistic crossbows.
quotes: A crossbow takes (5 – Strength) minutes to reload.
No character may discharge a bolt more than once per combat round.

entries.title: Combat Statistics (Grogs)
entries.summary: Pre-calculated combat statistics for common weapons under stated assumptions about Ability, Characteristics and encumbrance, to save time when building grogs.
quotes: It is often tedious to calculate combat statistics for a grog.

entries.title: Equipment Availability
entries.summary: Defines the historical periods (ancient, early medieval, high and late medieval) and regional availability used in the weapon and armor tables, so equipment can be matched to the saga's era.
quotes: The high period begins in the 11th century and lasts until the end of the 13th.

entries.title: Quality of Arms and Armor
entries.summary: Summarizes how shoddy, superior and excellent quality affects weapons, shields and armor, including breakage of shoddy items and the Protection, Attack and Defense bonuses of better ones.
quotes: Superior armor grants +1 to Protection.
Shoddy items break easily; they are destroyed after failing a single stress check

entries.title: New Weapon Rules
entries.summary: Weapons are now categorized as crushing, piercing or slashing by the injuries they cause, which does not change their statistics but may matter for how magic and other rules interact with them.
quotes: weapons are categorized as crushing, piercing, or slashing, according to the type of injuries they cause

related.text: ArM5 p.154 Edge of the Razor

entries.title: Primitive and Blunted Weapons
entries.summary: Stone weapons have reduced Damage modifiers, and slashing or piercing weapons blunted for tournaments reduce their Damage modifier further.
quotes: Subtract 3 from the Damage modifier of a blunted weapon.

entries.title: Option: Try Using the Other End
entries.summary: Optional rule making the order of damage categories in the weapon table significant: the first is the normal mode and using the second applies an Attack penalty.
quotes: Apply a –1 Attack penalty if it is used to deal its other damage type, due to awkwardness.

entries.title: Melee Weapon Table
entries.summary: Consolidated table of melee weapons and shields with Ability, Initiative, Attack, Defense, Damage, Strength, Load, Cost, availability, damage type and damage levels, with notes on nets, whips, long swords and polearms.
quotes: A net or whip may be used to trip, grapple, or disarm using wielder's Single Weapon + Weapon Attack Bonus in lieu of Brawl.
A halberd or pole arm may be used to unseat a rider.

entries.title: Missile Weapon Table
entries.summary: Consolidated table of thrown and missile weapons, bows and crossbows with Ability, Initiative, Attack, Defense, Damage, Range, Strength, Load, Cost, availability and damage type.
quotes: | Arbalest | Crossbow | 5 | 5 | 0 | 10 | 30 | –1 | 3 | Exp. | High | P | 2 | New |

entries.title: Option: The Clash of Weapons
entries.summary: Optional weapon-breakage rule: when an Attack Total exactly equals the Defense Total, a Strength + Ability contest decides whose weapon is at risk, and a breakage roll that fails costs the item a damage level.
quotes: Check for weapon breakage whenever the attacker's melee Attack Total exactly equals the defender's Defense Total.
Weapon Breakage: stress die + Weapon Ability vs. Ease Factor 9

entries.title: Using Crossbows
entries.summary: Updated crossbow rules: no untrained-use botch dice, the user's Strength does not add to Damage, spanning is an Extended Action, and a loaded crossbow can be shot as a fast action with the ready missiles option.
quotes: The user's Strength does not add to Damage for crossbows.
Spanning a crossbow is an Extended Action.

entries.title: Missile Weapon Descriptions
entries.summary: Describes the arbalest, heavy arbalest, crossbow and bows, including the number of rounds of Extended Action needed to span each type of crossbow.
quotes: To span a crossbow with a belt hook (the usual method) is a threeround Extended Action.

entries.title: Melee Weapon Descriptions
entries.summary: Describes weapons from the melee table and how they work, including nets and whips used for trip, grapple, disarm and unseat attempts, the halberd, infantry shield and how a bastard sword is treated one- and two-handed.
quotes: If used two-handed, treat it as a great sword.

entries.title: Expanded Armor Rules
entries.summary: Introduces an expanded set of historical armor types and rules for building armor from layers of different materials, compatible with the core armor statistics.

entries.title: Armor Materials
entries.summary: The expanded armor material categories replace those in the core rules while remaining compatible with their statistics.
quotes: The following categories expand and supersede those described on page 176 of ArM5.

entries.title: Inexpensive Materials
entries.summary: Defines padded armor and boiled leather as the inexpensive armor material categories, and which similar materials use the same statistics.
quotes: Also use these statistics for similar, semiresilient materials like rawhide, or even faerie armor made of tree bark.

entries.title: Standard Materials
entries.summary: Defines reinforced armor, rigid scale and metal scale as the standard armor material categories.
quotes: Metal scale includes all kinds of metal lamellar.

entries.title: Weapon Table Key
entries.summary: Explains each column of the melee and missile weapon tables, including untrained weapon use, minimum Strength, Load, cost, availability, damage types and damage levels.
quotes: add three extra botch dice unless the weapon is a crossbow

entries.title: Expensive Materials
entries.summary: Defines mail, plate, and plate and mail as the expensive armor material categories, with notes on when each appeared historically and that the complex armor rules do not cover 15th-century full plate.
quotes: The complex armor design rules do not cover 15th-century full plate.

entries.title: Expanded Armor Table
entries.summary: Tables giving Protection and Load for each armor material in each garment type, plus surcoats, greaves and helmets, which are added together to get a character's total Protection and Load.
quotes: Retain fractions until the end of the calculation and then round up to the next whole number.

entries.title: Armor Outfittings
entries.summary: Armor is built from three components (the armor itself, surcoat or greaves, and helmet) whose statistics are added; explains the common outfittings and why some material and garment combinations are not available.
quotes: Full armor protects all four limbs as well as the torso and loins.

entries.title: Option: Penalty for Fighting Without a Helmet
entries.summary: Optional rule adding a botch die to melee Defense and Evasion rolls for characters who fight without head protection, since helmets add little to Protection directly.
quotes: add an extra botch die to melee Defense (and Evasion) rolls for any character so foolish as to fight without head protection

entries.title: Glossary of Armor Terms
entries.summary: Definitions of armor terms such as hauberk, haubergeon, cuirass, jerkin, gambeson and brigandine, used to read the armor tables, with a few notes on which statistics to use for certain armors.
quotes: Use the statistics for a metal scale cuirass.

entries.title: Option: Complex Armor Design
entries.summary: Optional procedure for designing armor from any combination of materials: for each material add the Protection of the body areas it covers, multiply by the material's Load Factor, then sum all materials and round up.
quotes: multiply it by the Load Factor for that material and retain any fraction to get the total Load of that material

entries.title: Complex Armor Design Table
entries.summary: Table giving, for each armor material, the Protection it provides on each body area and its Load Factor, for use with the complex armor design procedure.

entries.title: Naphtha Pots and Lighting Bombs
entries.summary: Rules for Egyptian incendiary, explosive and poison grenades, including the damage each kind does and how troops react to them.
quotes: Most pots contain a thick gel that burns for several minutes, doing +10 damage each turn to whatever the fuel touches.
Characters may face the naphtha with a Brave Personality trait roll against an Ease Factor of 5.

entries.title: Treatment of Wounds
entries.summary: Expands the core Wound Recovery roll by splitting the Chirurgy bonus into a First Aid bonus and a Palliative Care bonus.
quotes: Stamina + First Aid Bonus + Palliative Care Bonus + Recovery Modifiers + Magical Aid + stress die

entries.title: First Aid
entries.summary: First aid given within a day of injury adds a bonus to Wound Recovery, and a successful First Aid roll can also let a patient act as though his wounds were one category less serious for a day.
quotes: First Aid Bonus to Wound Recovery: (Chirurgy / 2)
First Aid Roll: Dexterity + Chirurgy + Recovery Modifiers + Magical Aid + stress die vs Improvement Ease Factor

entries.title: Palliative Care
entries.summary: Ongoing wound care adds a bonus to Wound Recovery; the combined Chirurgy bonus from first aid and palliative care is capped by the Chirurgy of the caregiver. Also covers how many patients can be cared for and how subordinates help.
quotes: Palliative Care Bonus to Wound Recovery: (Chirurgy / 2)
cannot exceed the Chirurgy Ability of the character supplying the palliative care

entries.title: The Four Humors and their correspondences
entries.summary: Defines the four humors (blood, choler, melancholy, phlegm) and includes a table linking each to a bodily force, age, season, element, quality and opposed humor. This is the basis for diagnosing complexion and prescribing treatments.

entries.title: Complexion
entries.summary: Explains complexion as a person's blend of humors, the four basic complexions, how people usually combine two or three, and why a physician must determine it first.
quotes: The four basic complexions are sanguine, choleric, melancholic, and phlegmatic.

entries.title: Physical Qualities of the Four Complexions
entries.summary: Table of stature, build, hair, pulse, appetite, digestion, urine, skin and dreams for sanguine, choleric, melancholic and phlegmatic complexions, used to diagnose a patient or describe a character.

entries.title: States of Ill-Health
entries.summary: Divides ill health into injuries, malformations and diseases, caused by non-naturals and contra-naturals, and says which kind of practitioner treats each.

entries.title: The Non-Naturals
entries.summary: Introduces the non-naturals (air, diet, exercise and rest, sleep, evacuation, emotions and sensory species) as the outside influences that determine humoral balance and health.

entries.title: Qualities of Common Foods
entries.summary: Lists common foods by whether they heat or cool and moisten or dry, for planning diets that counter a patient's dominant humor.

entries.title: Forms of Exercise
entries.summary: Lists examples of strenuous and mild exercise for prescribing a regimen.

entries.title: Effects of the Non-Naturals and Causes of Heat, Cold, Moisture and Dryness
entries.summary: Explains how excess heat, cold, moisture or dryness in the non-naturals harms the body, and tabulates the climate, diet, exercise, sleep, evacuation, emotion and sensory causes of each quality.
quotes: Any excess of a source of heat, cold, dryness, or moisture has a detrimental effect on the body.

entries.title: Emotional States
entries.summary: The five emotional states (gaudium, laetitia, tristitia, ira, timor), their effect on the humors and health, and their link to the emotion-affecting Mentem guidelines.

entries.title: The Contra-Naturals
entries.summary: Describes the contra-naturals that cause wounds, poison, vermin, malign celestial influences behind epidemics, and supernatural harm.

entries.title: Malformations
entries.summary: Malformations are structural disorders, mostly represented in play as Flaws or as effects of aging, and they cannot be cured by physicians or chirurgeons.
quotes: Malformations cannot be cured with either Medicine or Chirurgy.

entries.title: Flaws Representing Malformations
entries.summary: List of Minor and Major Flaws that stand in for malformations in game terms.

entries.title: Symptoms of humoral imbalance
entries.summary: Describes plethoras of quantity and quality and the characteristic symptoms of an excess of normal or morbid blood, choler, melancholy and phlegm, for diagnosis and for inventing diseases.

entries.title: Medical Seasonal Activities
entries.summary: Lists the care activities a medicus can combine in one season, and the ones that consume the whole season, with the number of patients served tied to the practitioner's Abilities. Characters who gain no experience from the chosen activities get Exposure experience instead.
quotes: A character can do two different activities from the following list in a season
Provide therapy for up to (Medicine) characters
Therapy for up to (5 x Medicine) characters

entries.title: Epidemiology and the Prognosis Total
entries.summary: Explains the design intent of the new disease rules: a physician's Medicine only helps a patient recover if the physician's Prognosis Total is high enough for the disease, so diseases are harder to cure than in the core rules.
quotes: the physician now has to have a sufficiently high Prognosis Total to have this effect

entries.title: Magical Assistance to Disease Recovery Rolls
entries.summary: Creo Corpus magic can add bonuses to Disease Recovery rolls, separate from the Prognosis Total. Diseases caused by possession require the magic to penetrate the possessing creature's Might.
quotes: These bonuses to disease recovery do not affect the Prognosis Total

entries.title: Diagnosis and Prognosis
entries.summary: Defines the Prognosis Total, a roll-free total compared against a disease's Severity that decides whether the physician's Medicine counts toward the patient's recovery, and how modifiers from diet, apothecary and chirurgeon feed into it. Also gives a separate Perception + Medicine roll for diagnosis alone.
quotes: Intelligence + Medicine + Diet modifier + Medication modifier + Surgery modifier
If the Prognosis Total is greater than the severity of the disease, then the medicus has sufficient skill to plan therapy for his patient
the physician should make a Perception + Medicine roll

entries.title: Therapy
entries.summary: Therapy is the day-to-day care that is resolved through the patient's Disease Recovery roll, including how many patients a physician can handle and how subordinates share his Prognosis. The Prognosis Total must be recalculated if apothecary or chirurgeon help is lost or the disease changes Severity.
quotes: Recovery Modifiers + Magical Aid + stress die
A physician can provide therapy to a number of patients at a time equal to his Medicine Ability

entries.title: Prevention of Disease (Regimens)
entries.summary: A physician can set a patient on a regimen that improves the patient's Living Conditions Modifier after a year, with the size of the bonus limited by the physician's Medicine and the number of clients. The bonus is lost if eucrasia is disrupted and takes a year to re-establish.
quotes: Clients = Physician's (Medicine x 5) Bonus to Living Conditions Modifier: +1 Minimum Medicine: 1
Single Client Bonus to Living Conditions Modifier: +3 Minimum Medicine: 7
Each physician can only manage a single regimen

entries.title: Regimens and Covenants
entries.summary: Gives the multiplier applied to Inhabitant points when covenfolk are kept on a regimen, making the diet expensive for the covenant's finances.
quotes: Increased to +2 | x2
A regimen cannot be instituted if the covenant is applying Emergency Savings to their food budget

entries.title: Surgery
entries.summary: Rules and table of Ease Factors for surgical procedures, each of which inflicts a wound on the patient but gives a bonus to the next Disease Recovery roll on success. Failure and botch results are described.
quotes: Dexterity + Chirurgy + Recovery Modifiers + stress die
the patient receives a +3 to his next Disease Recovery roll
Phlebotomy, cautery, and cupping can only affect the most trivial diseases (Severity 5 or less) on their own

entries.title: Nurses
entries.summary: Describes how a nurse can lead or assist in first aid, palliative care and, with some Medicine, therapy.
quotes: a nurse can act as the lead chirurgeon in both first aid and palliative care

entries.title: Surgical Intervention
entries.summary: When a Wound Recovery roll fails, a chirurgeon can attempt emergency surgery to stop the wound worsening, at the price of a permanent consequence that depends on the wound's severity. A failed or botched Surgery roll makes matters worse, and lists give the Flaws and Characteristics affected by the wound's location.
quotes: He must make a Surgery roll (see Surgery, above) against an Ease Factor of 9
Make an immediate Aging roll
Gain a Major Flaw appropriate to the type of wound

entries.title: Midwifery
entries.summary: Rules for resolving childbirth in play by treating labor as a pseudo-wound to the mother, with consequences for the baby as her condition changes.
quotes: The onset of labor is treated as a Medium Wound to the mother, except that Wound Recovery rolls are made every 2 hours
suffers a –2 penalty to his Chirurgy Ability

entries.title: The Practice of the Apothecary
entries.summary: Explains how Profession: Apothecary complements Medicine, and how a physician's constant access to an apothecary reduces the Disease Recovery penalty for lacking medicinals.
quotes: is reduced by the Profession: Apothecary Ability, although it cannot become a bonus
Profession: Apothecary is an adjunct to Medicine

entries.title: Medicinals
entries.summary: Defines the four degrees of strength of a medicinal and what each does to the body, and describes the effects of heating, moistening, drying and cooling medicines.
quotes: causes destruction or death of tissue
Medicinals of the fourth degree are all poisonous

entries.title: Pharmacy
entries.summary: Describes forms of medicinal preparation and gives a Dexterity + Profession: Apothecary roll, with an Ease Factor by duration, to determine how long a preserved ingredient keeps. Preservation can also extend the Duration of an Arcane Connection that is a plant or animal part.
quotes: Make an Dexterity + Profession: Apothecary roll
the Duration of the Arcane Connection is increased by one category
Only Arcane Connections that are plants or animal body parts can be extended in this manner by an apothecary

entries.title: The Apothecary's Store
entries.summary: An apothecary generates Labor Points each season he practises his trade, loses stock every year and through extra drains such as regimens, formulae and ligatures, and can avoid those drains by searching for specific ingredients with a stress roll modified by terrain, season and assistants.
quotes: Labor Points per Eligible Season: (Intelligence + Profession: Apothecary) x Wealth Multiplier
An apothecary's business loses 36 labor points every year
Per + Profession: Apothecary, against Ease Factor of 9

related.text: City & Guild Chapter Two: Labor, pp.37-40

entries.title: Childbearing
entries.summary: Resolves whether a birth succeeds by treating the delivering mother as having an imaginary wound with recovery rolls, with the baby losing Fatigue as it worsens; midwives, physicians, relics and Creo Corpus spells can help.
quotes: treat the delivering mother as if she had a Medium Wound
If the baby loses five Fatigue levels, it dies.

entries.title: Debilitation
entries.summary: Diseases and poisons require a Stamina check against an Ease Factor set by the agent; failure means a wound treated with Medicine that then recovers by the usual rules.
quotes: Anyone exposed to a debilitating agent, whether poison or a cause of disease, must make a Stamina check against an Ease Factor set by the cause of the disease.

entries.title: Diseases
entries.summary: How diseases are modelled: humoral imbalances or disease spirits, handled via aging or debilitation, with Ease Factors indicating how much of a population is affected.
quotes: a disease with an Ease Factor of six will afflict about half of the population

entries.title: Disease Table
entries.summary: Table of four sample diseases with the excess humor and symptoms of each.

entries.title: Poisons
entries.summary: Poison Ease Factors have a minimum and a maximum, and poisons can inflict fatal wounds from the start.
quotes: The Ease Factor for the initial Stamina check is at least 3

entries.title: Poison Table
entries.summary: Table of sample poisons with their Ease Factor and the wound they cause.

entries.title: Disease (overview)
entries.summary: Explains diseases as humoral imbalance, how they corrupt the faculties if they persist, which Ability treats them, and how supernatural beings may cause them.
quotes: The treatment of diseases is almost exclusively the purview of the Medicine Ability

entries.title: Describing a Disease
entries.summary: Defines the statistics of a disease: Severity, Interval between recovery rolls, and the Stable and Improvement Ease Factors.
quotes: Diseases can be Minor, Serious, Major, or Critical

entries.title: Contracting a Disease
entries.summary: How a character is exposed to disease and rolls to avoid it, what a failure or botch means, and the incubation period.
quotes: Disease Avoidance roll: Stamina + Living Conditions Modifier + (Corpus/5) + Wound Penalty + stress die

entries.title: Disease Table and Modifiers to Severity
entries.summary: Tables giving base Severity and Disease Penalty for each disease level, and the Severity modifiers for Interval and for Stable and Improvement Ease Factors.

entries.title: Disease Progression and Recovery
entries.summary: How Disease Penalties work, how Disease Recovery rolls make a disease worse, stable or better, lifelong diseases, resting while ill, and the Disease Recovery roll formula.
quotes: If a character fails to meet the Stable Ease Factor, then the disease level worsens by one.
Stamina + Medicine + (Corpus/5) + Wound Penalty + Recovery Modifiers (see below) + stress die

entries.title: Make Your Own Plague
entries.summary: Guidance for building a new disease or a disease-causing spell: pick symptoms, translate them into penalties or Flaws, then derive severity, interval and Ease Factors.

entries.title: Crises (critical diseases)
entries.summary: Rules for a character with a Critical disease: twice-daily Disease Recovery rolls, death on a very low total, improvement on meeting the Stable Ease Factor, and a permanent aging point for survivors.
quotes: The player must make two Disease Recovery rolls each day (at sunrise and sunset) that the character remains in Crisis.

entries.title: Calculating the Severity of a Disease
entries.summary: Procedure for working out a disease's Severity from its base level plus Interval and Ease Factor modifiers, with a worked example.
quotes: The Improvement Ease Factor must always be greater than the Stable Ease Factor.

entries.title: Some Common Diseases (sample disease catalogue)
entries.summary: Catalogue of ready-made diseases, each with its level, humor, Severity, Stable and Improvement Ease Factors, Interval, cause and symptoms or Flaws, including special rules for leprosy, convulsions, tumors and others.

entries.title: Poisons
entries.summary: Fourth-degree substances act as poisons, with different effects for each quality. Poison manufacture falls under Profession: Apothecary, and only simple poisons can be made without knowing the correct formula.
quotes: Only simple poisons (those that inflict a Light Wound, and that have an Ease Factor of 6 or less to resist the damage

entries.title: Disease in Towns (Humors and Exposure)
entries.summary: Explains the humoral theory of disease in Mythic Europe, how Medicine and Hermetic spells diagnose and treat it, and how a storyguide decides when town dwellers are tested for exposure or contract disease through an Aging Crisis.
quotes: Diagnosing and prescribing the correct treatment for a disease is represented by the Medicine Ability (ArM5, pages 66, 179, 180).
Precisely how often a character must be tested for exposure to sources of humoral imbalance is at the discretion of the storyguide.

related.text: ArM5 p.130 Intellego and Creo Corpus spells

entries.title: The Ague
entries.summary: A fever disease tied to urban bad air; a failed Stamina roll means the character contracts it and takes a wound, with the fever type determining the severity.
quotes: a Stamina roll against an Ease Factor of 3, 6, or 9 (depending upon the strength of the bad air source) is failed

entries.title: St. Anthony's Fire
entries.summary: A disease caused by a minor demon lodged in the victim's intestines; it is a magical attack resisted with Magic Resistance and inflicts an escalating wound each season until exorcised.
quotes: a Stamina roll against an Ease Factor of 9 is failed
a Light Wound in the first season, escalating to a Fatal Wound in the fifth

entries.title: Tarantism
entries.summary: A disease from a faerie tarantula bite that forces seasonal bouts of dancing; resisted with Stamina rolls and cured by hearing the tarentella.
quotes: unless a Stamina roll is made against an Ease Factor of 9
Once per season a Stamina Roll against an Ease Factor of 3 (or 6 in summer) must be made for each afflicted character.

entries.title: Childbed Fever
entries.summary: A demon-borne danger when a character gives birth; a Stamina roll avoids it, and failure causes a wound, worse with birthing complications. It is a magical attack resisted with Magic Resistance.
quotes: When a character gives birth a Stamina roll against an Ease Factor of 6 is made.

entries.title: The Bloody Flux
entries.summary: A disease from cold, wet conditions common in towns and armies; a failed Stamina roll against an Ease Factor tied to the excess of phlegm causes a wound of matching severity.
quotes: If a Stamina roll against an Ease Factor of 3, 6, or 9 (depending upon the extent of the excess phlegm) is failed

entries.title: Worms
entries.summary: A disease of an excess of the blood humor; a failed Stamina roll means infection, followed by seasonal Stamina rolls that can inflict a wound.
quotes: A character with an excess of blood contracts worms if a Stamina roll against an Ease Factor of 6 is failed.

entries.title: Abscesses (Deprivation Wounds)
entries.summary: Links the colour of pustules to the missing humor and to the severity of the Deprivation Wound that produced them during famine.
quotes: Black pustules indicate a lack of yellow bile, and develop from Incapacitating Deprivation Wounds.

entries.title: Digging for Arsenic Is Dangerous
entries.summary: Rules for protecting oneself while harvesting arsenic: precautions determine whether the character is automatically poisoned or must make a Dexterity-based roll.
quotes: against an Ease Factor of 5, +1 per dose

entries.title: Magical Medicine and Disease Recovery
entries.summary: Explains how a bonus to Disease Recovery rolls from a healing device changes the odds of a severe disease worsening or improving, and that ritual cures cannot be put into enchanted items.
quotes: with a +6 bonus to Disease Recovery rolls he has an even chance of improving, and has only a one in a hundred chance of getting worse

entries.title: Prognosis Total for Diagnosing Disease
entries.summary: Shows how a character with Medicine diagnoses a disease by comparing a Prognosis Total (with no die roll) to the disease's severity, using the Diet, Medication and Surgery modifiers, with an example for Saint Anthony's Fire.
quotes: Prognosis Total: Intelligence + Medicine + Diet modifier + Medication modifier + Surgery modifier
There is no die roll added to the Prognosis Total.

entries.title: Treating Disease: Aid, Magic and Divine Cures
entries.summary: Describes how mundane care, medicine, Intellego Corpus diagnosis, Perdo Vim and holy power or relics can help victims of a demon-caused disease, including the modifier that better living conditions give to the Disease Recovery roll.
quotes: Better living conditions, healthier food, and fresh and plentiful water add +1 to the Disease Recovery roll.

related.text: Realms of Power: the Divine pp.48, 60, 87

entries.title: Dealing with Disease (Avoidance, Recovery and Crisis)
entries.summary: A short summary of the Art & Academe disease system: Disease Avoidance rolls, severities and their penalties, intervals, Disease Recovery rolls against Stable and Improvement Ease Factors, Crisis, and a simpler Stamina-check alternative.
quotes: Disease Avoidance Roll: Stamina + Living Condition Modifier + (Corpus/5) + Wound Penalty + stress die
Disease Recovery Roll: Stamina + Medicine + (Corpus/5) + Wound Penalty + Recovery Modifiers
If the roll fails to beat the Stable Ease Factor, the disease worsens in severity.

entries.title: Plant Diseases in the 13th Century
entries.summary: Explains how plants fall ill naturally from nutritional imbalance or unnaturally from magical, infernal or divine agencies, and gives severity, Stable and Improve numbers and timelines for sun scorch, grubs, kambros, mold and necrosis.
quotes: Critical Disease, Severity 15 Stable 12, Improve 18, Interval: Hour
Mold is a determined ailment and will destroy an Individual-sized plant in 7 days.

entries.title: Scrofula (the King's Evil)
entries.summary: Rules for catching scrofula in crowded, hot-weather towns: a Stamina roll resisted against an Ease Factor that varies with the season, a Medium wound if caught, the Disfigured Flaw in advanced cases, and cure by Medicine, Creo Corpus magic or the King of France's touch.
quotes: It requires a Stamina roll against an Ease Factor of 6 or 9 (depending upon the time of year) to avoid catching the disease, which inflicts a Medium wound.

entries.title: The Fen Ague
entries.summary: Swamp disease contracted by travelers in the Cotentin marshes on a failed Stamina roll, causing a Heavy Wound with fever symptoms and curable by Hermetic magic.
quotes: Travelers foolish enough to risk the Cotentin swamps must make a Stamina roll against an Ease Factor of 3.

entries.title: Groups
entries.summary: Basic rules for forming combat groups: size limit, roughly comparable Combat Totals, a vanguard, an optional leader, and when a group splits or reforms.
quotes: Groups are handled together for combat purposes, and may consist of one to six characters, inclusive.

entries.title: Group Damage
entries.summary: A group deals its damage once per member, distributed as evenly as possible among the opposing group, with the vanguard taking at least as many blows and its wound penalties applying to the group.
quotes: The vanguard must always take at least as many blows as every other member of the group.

entries.title: Untrained Group
entries.summary: A group of similar-ability characters whose combat statistics are simply those of the vanguard.
quotes: Combat statistics are as for the vanguard.

entries.title: Trained Group
entries.summary: Groups that have trained together get a leader, a limit on size from Leadership, and a bonus from the other members' combat abilities capped by the leader's Leadership, applied to either Attack or Defense.
quotes: The maximum number of fighters that can be coordinated is equal to the leader's Leadership score.

entries.title: Defender
entries.summary: Characters (such as a magus with shield grogs) can be protected by defenders who fight as a group and the defended is only harmed if they fail.
quotes: The number of characters defended may not exceed the number of characters defending.

entries.title: Defenders Without Groups
entries.summary: Sidebar allowing defenders even when the group rules are not used.
quotes: A defended character cannot be attacked until all his defenders have been incapacitated.

entries.title: Splitting Groups
entries.summary: Several attacking groups can try to break a defending group apart with an attack resolved on Attack Advantage rather than damage, dividing it evenly.
quotes: Groups may only try to split their opponents' groups in melee combat.

entries.title: Combat: Complex Example
entries.summary: Worked example of group combat between a trained and an untrained group, showing the group bonus, re-rolled Initiative ties, Wound Penalties and disengaging.

entries.title: The Drill Sergeant
entries.summary: The drill sergeant trains the grogs to fight as a trained group by teaching a Martial Ability each year, keeps order and administers punishments, and needs Leadership and Teaching.
quotes: This involves providing a season of teaching in a Martial Ability (usually Single Weapon) over the course of each year.

entries.title: Accelerated Group Training
entries.summary: A leader rolls to shorten the time a group needs to practice together before it counts as a trained group, against an Ease Factor set by how much training time is available; failure delays the group until season's end and a botch wastes the season.
quotes: Stress die + Communication + Leadership
When the training period is complete, they can function as a trained group (see ArM5, page 173).

entries.title: Putting Together Your Team
entries.summary: A grog expedition needs a full complement of five roles, and the size of a trained group is capped by the leader's Leadership, with a limit on how far apart the members' Combat Totals can be.
quotes: An individual can only lead a band of grogs as a trained group equal in size to his score in the Leadership Ability.
no more than a 5 point difference between any of the Combat Totals

entries.title: Commanding Larger Groups
entries.summary: A leader can command a group larger than his Leadership score through subordinates who command their own men, at the cost of higher Ease Factors for whole-group Leadership rolls and commands that take his whole action.
quotes: have Ease Factors 3 higher than normal
A leader can usually only have a number of men under his command equal to his Leadership score.

entries.title: Dux, the Leader
entries.summary: The dux coordinates the band in combat, runs the expedition day to day, and is the liaison for orders from the magi; a good Leadership score is essential.
quotes: an essential feature is a good score in the Leadership Ability

entries.title: Optio, the Second in Command
entries.summary: The optio ensures the leader's orders are carried out and takes over if the leader falls, so should have the second-best Leadership and complementary skills.
quotes: The optio should have the second-best Leadership score in the unit.

entries.title: Antesignanus, the Vanguard
entries.summary: The vanguard stands at the front of any fight and is the most likely to be wounded, so toughness Virtues matter; combining the vanguard and leader roles risks the whole trained group dissolving if he falls.
quotes: it dissolves into an untrained group immediately

entries.title: Immune, the Specialist
entries.summary: The immune is the team's specialist, chosen to suit the expedition (commonly a chirurgeon); one without basic combat skills cannot be part of the trained group.
quotes: If an immune does not have basic combat skills, he cannot be a member of the trained group.

entries.title: Signifer, the Legate
entries.summary: The signifer looks after the troop's internal tensions, pay and morale, speaks for the magi to mundanes, and is chosen for social skills such as Folk Ken and Carouse.
quotes: the signifer takes care of the internal tensions of the troop

entries.title: Accelerated Group Training
entries.summary: A good leader can train a group to fight together in less than a season by making a Communication + Leadership roll against an Ease Factor set by the available training time; trainees still gain experience only at season's end.
quotes: Shorten Training Time: Communication + Leadership + stress die

entries.title: The Leader's Actions
entries.summary: Issuing orders is usually a fast action and the leader acts at the same point in the sequence as the group; a group member who does something other than attack is not counted in the group's combat bonus or damage multiplier.
quotes: Issuing orders to command a group in combat is usually a fast action.

entries.title: Morale and Discipline
entries.summary: Introduces optional rules that moderately weaken groups while making the leader more important, with both Discipline and Morale being tested in battle.
quotes: Effective group tactics require both discipline and morale.

entries.title: Discipline
entries.summary: A group rolls Discipline as a reaction when tempted to break formation; the total is based on the leader's Presence and Leadership, with a bonus from a uniformly Loyal group, and a table of example Ease Factors. Failure leaves the group disordered.
quotes: Group Discipline: leader's Presence + leader's Leadership + stress die

entries.title: Morale
entries.summary: Groups make Morale rolls as reactions when bad things happen in battle; failure disorders the group and failure while already disordered routs it. A table gives example Ease Factors and a uniformly Brave group gets a bonus.
quotes: Group Morale: leader's Presence + leader's Leadership + stress die

entries.title: Disordered Groups
entries.summary: A disordered trained group functions as an untrained one, and a disordered untrained group lands only half its hits; a disordered group that fails a Morale check is routed.
quotes: A trained group that is disordered functions as an untrained group.

entries.title: Routed Groups
entries.summary: A routed group tries to disengage from all opponents and flee, and its members often scatter once clear; a group routs when it is already disordered and fails a Morale check.
quotes: A group can become routed if it is already disordered and then fails a Morale check.

entries.title: Rallying a Group
entries.summary: The leader may rally a disordered or routed group as an action with a Presence + Leadership roll against an Ease Factor depending on how the group is engaged and its casualties; success improves its status by one step.
quotes: Rally a Group: Presence + Leadership + stress die

entries.title: Groups With No Leader
entries.summary: Under the optional rules a group that loses its vanguard or leader can keep fighting, with rolls to replace the vanguard or assume leadership, though it automatically fails Morale and Discipline checks while leaderless.
quotes: Replace a Vanguard in Combat: leader's Presence + leader's Leadership + stress die vs. Ease Factor 9
Assume Leadership in Combat: Presence + Leadership + stress die vs. Ease Factor 9

entries.title: Trained Group and Mounted Bonuses for a Knightly Band
entries.summary: Shows how a band of companions fights as a trained group, the vanguard gaining a combat bonus from the others, and that mounted combatants add a bonus to Attack and Defense.
quotes: each receive a +3 bonus to their Attack and Defense Totals
