entries.title: Warping (Hermetic Dangers)
entries.summary: Points to the full Warping rules in Long Term Events and notes that magi gain a Warping Point for each zero on botch dice when they botch a spell.
quotes: Note that magi gain one Warping Point for every zero on the botch dice when they botch a spell.

entries.title: Warping
entries.summary: Defines the Warping Score, advanced with Warping Points like an Ability, and gives the table of Warping Points needed per score.
quotes: To increase the Warping Score by one point, a character needs five times the new score extra Warping Points.

entries.title: Gaining Warping Points
entries.summary: Lists the four separate sources of Warping Points, all of which stack.
quotes: Living in a strong (6 or higher) supernatural aura.

entries.title: Warping from Living in Strong Auras
entries.summary: Table of Warping Points gained per period by aura strength and how much time is spent in the aura; characters whose own powers come from that realm are exempt.
quotes: Auras of over five points have an effect on anyone living within them

entries.title: Warping from Powerful Supernatural Effects
entries.summary: A Warping Point is gained from being subjected to a powerful supernatural effect not created by or specifically designed for you; sixth magnitude and higher Hermetic spells count.
quotes: any Hermetic spell of sixth magnitude or higher counts

entries.title: Warping from Constant Supernatural Effects
entries.summary: Characters continuously under supernatural effects gain Warping Points over time regardless of effect strength; explains what counts as constant, exceptions such as Parma Magica, and a summary table of effect types.
quotes: A character who is constantly under the influence of one or more active supernatural effects gains one Warping Point per year for each effect.

entries.title: Warping from Supernatural Botches
entries.summary: Botching the roll to invoke a supernatural effect gives Warping Points equal to the number of zeros on the botch dice.
quotes: she gains one Warping Point for every zero on the botch dice.

entries.title: Effects of Warping
entries.summary: What a rising Warping Score does to a character: more prone to Twilight for magi, and for mundane characters a progression of Minor Flaws, a supernatural Minor Virtue and then Major Flaws.
quotes: At a Warping Score of 6, and every point thereafter, the character gains a Major Flaw appropriate to the main sources of the warping.

entries.title: Warping and Non-Humans
entries.summary: Mundane creatures and things can be warped, but the storyguide just describes effects; creatures with a Might score are immune to Warping.
quotes: Creatures with a Might score are absolutely immune to warping.

entries.title: Warped Plants
entries.summary: Rules for Warping in plants: short-lived plants escape it, while older perennials and trees gain Minor Flaws (and Virtues) from warping, with common Flaw examples.
quotes: Annual and biennial plants escape such effects by virtue of their short lifespans, but perennial plants that are five years or older possess a Minor Flaw from warping

related.text: Realms of Power: Magic p.78 Warping of animals

entries.title: A Note on Warping by Enchanted Devices
entries.summary: Clarifies that level modifications such as Penetration, uses per day and triggers are not counted when working out whether an enchanted effect warps its targets.
quotes: Modifications to the level of an effect—including Penetration, effect frequency, environmental trigger, linked trigger and effect use—are not used to determine whether or not an effect causes warping to its targets through the power of the magical effect.

entries.title: Warping from Repeated Instant Transportation
entries.summary: Transportation effects of high level give a Warping point at every casting; after several castings the target gains a Minor Flaw, again after more, and after a very large number of transits a Minor Virtue. Inanimate objects are warped too, and there are no firm rules for what that does.
quotes: if a person, animal, or object is affected 5 times or more, it will suffer a Minor Flaw (ArM5, page 168), and another after 15 castings
Should one target experience 75 or more transits, it also accumulates a Minor Virtue.

entries.title: Wizard's Twilight
entries.summary: Wizard's Twilight is the Hermetic reaction to Warping, described in the following sections on entering, comprehending, living through and the effects of Twilight.
quotes: Wizard's Twilight is unique to Hermetic magic.

entries.title: Entering Twilight
entries.summary: When a maga gains two or more Warping Points from a single event she rolls Twilight Avoidance against her Warping Score; failure or a botch sends her into Twilight, and she may choose not to resist.
quotes: TWILIGHT AVOIDANCE: Stamina + Concentration + Vim Form Bonus + stress die vs. Warping Score + Number of Warping Points gained
Whenever a maga gains two or more Warping Points from a single event, rather than from prolonged exposure

entries.title: Comprehending Twilight
entries.summary: A maga in Twilight rolls to comprehend it against her Warping Score; the Warping Score sets the base real-world time in Twilight, which shortens with a good comprehension roll and lengthens on a botch.
quotes: TWILIGHT COMPREHENSION: Intelligence + Enigmatic Wisdom + stress die vs. Warping Score + stress die
BOTCH DICE: 1 + 1 per Warping Point gained to trigger the Twilight
TWILIGHT TIME: Intelligence + stress die vs. Warping Score + stress die

entries.title: Effects of Twilight
entries.summary: Every Twilight gives extra Warping Points from a simple die plus a Twilight Scar and a good effect (increased knowledge, new Virtue, new spell) if comprehended, or a bad effect (lost knowledge, new Flaw, lost spells) if not.
quotes: The maga gains that many Warping Points, in addition to the points that triggered the Twilight.
Increased Knowledge: A number of experience points in an Art, Magic Theory, or Enigmatic Wisdom, equal to twice the number of Warping Points gained.
Lost Knowledge: Lose two experience points for every Warping Point gained in an Art, Magic Theory, or Enigmatic Wisdom.

entries.title: During Twilight
entries.summary: Describes what a maga experiences in Twilight and how her body behaves in the outside world; if it remains it is immune to magic, damage, aging and hunger but cannot perform magic.
quotes: it is completely immune to magic, mundane damage, aging, and hunger

entries.title: Twilight Example
entries.summary: Worked example of avoiding, failing to comprehend and recovering from a Twilight caused by a spell botch.
quotes: Darius has a Stamina of 0, Concentration 3, and a Vim bonus of 2.

entries.title: Advanced Group Combat
entries.summary: Introduces optional rules that add tactical depth to the core Group Combat rules, first printed in Lords of Men, which troupes may use or skip as drama and preference dictate.
quotes: The rules in this section expand the Group Combat rules in ArM5 to add a bit more tactical depth.

entries.title: The Leader's Actions
entries.summary: A group leader gets one command roll per round without spending his action, and a member who stays in the group but does something other than attack is not counted for the group's combat bonus or damage.
quotes: A group leader can make one command-related die roll per round without using his action for that round.

entries.title: Morale and Discipline
entries.summary: Optional rules that weaken groups somewhat but make the leader important even for untrained groups, by requiring discipline and morale checks in battle.
quotes: Effective group tactics require both discipline and morale.

entries.title: Discipline
entries.summary: A Discipline roll, which takes no action, is needed when a group is tempted to break formation; failure leaves the group Disordered. The roll uses the leader's Presence and Leadership, with example Ease Factors by event.
quotes: stress die + Leader's Presence + Leader's Leadership
If a Discipline roll fails, the group temporarily becomes Disordered.

entries.title: Morale
entries.summary: Groups make Morale rolls, which take no action, when bad things happen on the battlefield; failure makes the group Disordered and a failure while already Disordered routs it. The group may gain a bonus from its members' Brave scores, and example Ease Factors are listed.
quotes: stress die + Leader's Pre + Leader's Leadership
A group that fails a morale check becomes Disordered.

entries.title: Disordered Groups
entries.summary: Effects of a Disordered group: a trained group functions as an untrained one, an untrained Disordered group can only land part of its attacks, and a further failed Morale check routs it.
quotes: A trained group that is Disordered functions as an untrained group.

entries.title: Routed Groups
entries.summary: A routed group has lost its will to fight and tries to Disengage and flee, possibly scattering; a group is routed if already Disordered and it fails a Morale check.
quotes: A group can become Routed if it is already Disordered and then fails a Morale check.

entries.title: Rallying a Group
entries.summary: The leader spends an action on a Presence + Leadership roll to improve a Routed group to Disordered or a Disordered group to normal, with Ease Factors set by the group's situation and raised by casualties.
quotes: Presence + Leadership + stress Die

entries.title: Groups With No Leader
entries.summary: Optional rules for groups that lose their vanguard or leader: a group without a vanguard cannot attack but uses its best member's Defense, replacing a vanguard or taking over command is done by a Presence + Leadership roll, and a leaderless group automatically fails Morale and Discipline checks.
quotes: Leader's Presence + Leadership vs. Ease Factor 9
Presence + Leadership vs. Ease Factor 9
A group with no leader automatically fails any future Morale or Discipline checks.

entries.title: Medieval Armies
entries.summary: The categories of troops in an army, the Living Conditions and disease cost of campaigning, the usual mix of units, and the baggage units an army needs, with a Leadership penalty when they are missing.
quotes: Characters suffer a –1 Living Conditions modifier for each year during which they spend at least one season in a campaigning army.
For every ten units in an army (rounded up) the army also needs one unit of baggage.

related.text: Art & Academe p.46 Disease Avoidance Roll

entries.title: Vassals
entries.summary: A table of the standard combat groups of each troop type a lord can raise from his household and vassals by rank, how losses are replaced, and the use of scutage.
quotes: the table below shows the average number of standard combat groups (each consisting of five fully equipped men)

entries.title: Mercenary Budget
entries.summary: How much a noble can spend on mercenaries by rank and wealth without lowering his standard of living, the Allied Troops Table, mercenary unit costs, and how a character may borrow against his income for a larger budget.
quotes: A character who is Poor may not do this.
A character who is average may become Poor and in exchange borrow five times the average mercenary budget of someone of his class in coin.

related.text: Covenants Chapter Five (cost of an armed force)

entries.title: Mercenary Units
entries.summary: A table of the cost in Mythic Pounds and experience level of typical mercenary combat groups.
quotes: The table below lists the costs of typical mercenary combat groups.

entries.title: Heroic Endeavors
entries.summary: The overall approach to playing a battle as a series of vignettes with a player character as the decisive force, using the standard or optional combat rules.
quotes: Battles are played as a series of vignettes, each with a player character as the decisive force.

related.text: LoM Chapter Nine: Optional Combat Rules

entries.title: Territorial Advantage
entries.summary: Each army generates a Deployment Total, and the difference gives territorial advantage; commanders may delegate the roll to a lieutenant, and the battlefield's features and auras affect events.
quotes: Deployment Total: Intelligence + Area Lore + Stress Die
Territorial Advantage: Deployment Total – Enemy Deployment Total

related.text: Realms of Power: The Infernal p.10

entries.title: The Flow of Battle
entries.summary: The four-step sequence for running a battle: territorial advantage, weight of numbers, a battlefield event for each player character, and deciding victory.
quotes: The Weight of Numbers modifier is determined and assigned.

entries.title: Weight of Numbers
entries.summary: A bonus or penalty to event totals from the ratio of army sizes counted in standard combat groups, recalculated as losses mount.
quotes: The size of an army is measured in standard combat groups of five individuals.

entries.title: Battlefield Events
entries.summary: How a battle is broken into pivotal events, each with a Battle Ease Factor that rises as the battle goes on, which the focal character must meet with an Event Total built from an Event Bonus of Maneuver, Enemy and Size.
quotes: Event Total: Stamina + Leadership + Territorial Advantage + Weight of Numbers Bonus + Event Bonus
Event Bonus: Maneuver + Enemy + Size
Unless otherwise stated, each battlefield event lasts five combat rounds.

entries.title: Maneuver
entries.summary: The kinds of action a battlefield event demands, each with an Event Bonus value and win conditions: Defend, Attack, Run the Gauntlet, Take and Heroic Gesture.
quotes: If the leading character dies during a Heroic Gesture, the event is won and the player should describe how that death secures victory.

entries.title: Size
entries.summary: How many opposing combat groups a battlefield event involves, each option with an Event Bonus value, and how Weight of Numbers changes group sizes.
quotes: The Size of a battlefield event describes the number of combat groups the characters must defeat before they can win the event.

entries.title: Enemy
entries.summary: The kind of opponents in a battlefield event, from levies to special foes to attacking the baggage, each with an Event Bonus value; attacking baggage costs Reputation.
quotes: Characters choosing this Enemy option gain 1 experience point towards a bad Reputation.

entries.title: Wounds and Attrition
entries.summary: Losses to the defeated side after each event, the losing commander's Morale roll and rally attempt, and how player characters can rally a failing army.
quotes: the commander of the losing side must make a Morale roll (see Chapter Nine: Optional Combat Rules) against Ease Factor 6.
On a failure, the commander can attempt to rally his forces (Ease Factor 9) at the beginning of the next event.

related.text: LoM Chapter Nine: Optional Combat Rules (Morale)

entries.title: Example Battlefield Events
entries.summary: Worked examples of battlefield events, each showing the Maneuver, Size and Enemy chosen, the resulting Event Bonus and how the event plays out.
quotes: Each round in which a light wound is inflicted on them prevents them advancing, otherwise they advance 15 paces each round.

entries.title: The Aftermath of Battle
entries.summary: Rewards of victory in Confidence Points and Reputation, treatment of the wounded and their ability to travel, and the fate of prisoners by rank.
quotes: A successful battle earns the victorious characters one Confidence Point for each successful battlefield event whether they took part in that event or not.
The leader of the army also gains 1 experience point towards an appropriate Reputation.

entries.title: Standard Combat Groups
entries.summary: Combat statistics for standard five-person groups of knights, serjeants, infantry, archers, levies and baggage, and which are trained or untrained.
quotes: Each group is assumed to be five individuals.
a group that serves together for a season is treated as trained thereafter

entries.title: Siegecraft
entries.summary: Introduces the abstract siege rules, which resolve the capture and defense of castles and fortified towns through military events rather than negotiation, and leaves the final fall of a castle to troupe judgment.
quotes: It is for the troupe to determine when a castle finally becomes indefensible.

entries.title: Magic on the Battlefield
entries.summary: Sets the Concentration rolls needed to cast spells amid a battle and explains how the Group and Boundary targets can be scaled up to affect units or battlefield areas.
quotes: Concentration roll against an Ease Factor of 9 in order to cast spells
Boosting the spell level by one magnitude increases the diameter to around 300 paces.

entries.title: Example Battle
entries.summary: A worked example of resolving a battle through a series of battlefield events, showing how the lead character's total, the Weight of Numbers modifier, the Ease Factor and the Event Bonus fit together.
quotes: He needs an Event Bonus of +2 to reach the Ease Factor.

entries.title: Describing Castles
entries.summary: Introduces the three characteristics (Garrison, Defenses, Supplies) that describe a castle for siege play, each with a quality and a check interval.
quotes: the lowest interval pertaining to a given castle determines how often key siege events are played out when the castle is besieged

entries.title: Castle Garrison
entries.summary: A castle's Garrison is rated by the number of combat groups in it, which sets both the check interval and the Weight of Numbers modifier used in siege rolls.
quotes: The castle Garrison is measured in combat groups

entries.title: Castle Defenses
entries.summary: Rates a castle's walls and earthworks by quality grade to give a Defense Bonus and check interval, and uses castle size to work out how many damage levels each of its four walls has.
quotes: Permanent defensive enchantments also add +1 to the overall Defense Bonus.
The castle's Defense Bonus is multiplied by the damage level modifier from the above table to determine the castle's damage levels.

entries.title: Castle Supplies
entries.summary: Rates the food and materials stored in a castle and its ability to resupply, giving a check interval and a Siege Conditions Bonus used when the castle is stockaded.
quotes: Supplies include the food, water, and raw materials stored inside the castle, and the ability of the castle to resupply itself.

entries.title: Life Under Siege
entries.summary: Explains what happens when a siege begins, how besieged castles and cities handle their populations, and the Living Conditions penalty for characters who spend a season under siege.
quotes: Characters under siege suffer from a –2 Living Conditions modifier each year in which at least one season is spent under siege.

entries.title: Stockade
entries.summary: Rules for starving out a castle: the besiegers must cover enough walls, and at each check interval the castle makes a supplies roll whose failure degrades its supplies and can bring disease or surrender.
quotes: Supplies Roll: Siege Conditions Bonus + stress die
Ease Factor: 3 + Garrison Weight of Numbers Modifiers + Number of Years Under Siege

entries.title: Making Supply Rolls
entries.summary: A shortcut for resolving a long siege quickly by rolling several supplies dice in one batch instead of one roll per interval.
quotes: roll four dice to quickly resolve the passing of a month

entries.title: Laying Siege
entries.summary: Describes how a siege is played as a series of decisive events at intervals set by the castle's weakest characteristic, and the attacking and defending options available to each side.
quotes: There are three options: undermining the walls, launching an artillery assault, or scaling the defenses.

entries.title: Siege Engines
entries.summary: Statistics table for ballistae, mangonels and trebuchets (initiative, attack, damage, crew, range, cost), with notes on reloading and how they are used against walls or troops.
quotes: Reloading these weapons takes two minutes and requires the whole crew.

entries.title: Troop Deployment
entries.summary: Each army designates units as miners, artillery or soldiers and assigns them among the four castle walls; an undefended wall may provoke an undefended escalade.
quotes: each army may nominate any number of its units as miners, artillery, or soldiers

entries.title: Undermining
entries.summary: Siege event in which miners tunnel under a chosen wall and burn the supports; attacker and castle each roll Intelligence plus Profession Sapper, and success lowers the castle's Defense Quality.
quotes: Mine Attack Total: Intelligence + Profession Sapper + Stress Die
Castle Defense: Intelligence + Profession Sapper + Defense Bonus + Stress Die
If the Mine Attack Total exceeds the Castle Defense, the mine attack is successful.

entries.title: New Abilities
entries.summary: Defines the Abilities Profession Sapper, Profession Siege Engineer and Siege Weapon, with what each covers and suggested specialities.
quotes: This Ability may not be used untrained

entries.title: Artillery
entries.summary: Siege event in which groups of mangonels and trebuchets batter walls; a successful attack inflicts damage levels on the wall, and a wall reduced to nothing no longer gives the castle its Defense Bonus there.
quotes: Artillery Attack: Intelligence + Siege Weapon Ability + Engine Attack Bonus + Stress Die
Castle Defense: Intelligence + Profession Siege Engineer + Defense Bonus + Stress Die

entries.title: Escalade
entries.summary: Siege event in which attackers scale the walls, resolved with the battlefield event rules with modifications for garrison, defense bonus and wall breaches.
quotes: Each victory by the attacking side reduces the castle's garrison characteristic by one step (beginning with the next siege event).

entries.title: Option: External Defenses
entries.summary: Optional rule letting a castle have outlying fortifications, bought as an extra minor castle, that attackers must capture first; they have their own Defense Bonus but share the main castle's supplies and garrison.
quotes: Such features have their own Defense Bonus but rely on the larger castle's supplies and garrison.

entries.title: Escalade Weapons and Defenses
entries.summary: Describes siege towers, ladders, cats and battering rams for attackers and incendiaries for defenders, and how to treat rams and boiling liquids with existing weapon and damage rules.
quotes: Battering rams are treated as bludgeons.

entries.title: Counterattack
entries.summary: The garrison may sally out to destroy specific enemy units, or fire its own siege engines at the enemy's engines; sorties are resolved as events with a fixed Battle Ease Factor and no Territorial Advantage or Weight of Numbers.
quotes: These actions have a Battle Ease Factor of 9.

entries.title: Example Siege Events
entries.summary: Three sample siege events (Scale the Ladders, Open the Gates, Take the Marshal), each with an Event Bonus built from the Man, Size and Enemy modifiers, showing how to frame a siege scene for a player character.
quotes: Event Bonus +7
(+2 Run the Gauntlet, +4 I Stand Alone, +2 Expensive)

entries.title: General Situational Modifiers
entries.summary: Guidance for assigning bonuses to Attack or Defense for battlefield circumstances, suggesting the values +1, +3 and +6 as slight, substantial and very significant edges, and phrasing modifiers as applying to the character in the unusual situation.
quotes: it is often easiest to simply choose between +1, +3, and +6

entries.title: Cover
entries.summary: Cover that actually stops attacks grants a Defense bonus against missile and melee attacks according to how much of the body is covered; it does not stack with concealment, only the higher bonus applies.
quotes: The Defense bonus from cover applies against both missile and melee attacks.
If a character has both cover and concealment, only the highest Defense bonus applies.

entries.title: Concealment, Darkness, and Invisibility
entries.summary: A table of concealment levels giving melee Attack and Defense bonuses (or Evasion) to hard-to-see characters, applying to both sides, plus extra botch dice for poor visibility and a pointer to the detailed invisibility rules.
quotes: These bonuses and penalties apply to both the attacker and the defender.

related.text: Houses of Hermes: Societates pp.32-33 Invisibility in combat

entries.title: Higher Ground
entries.summary: Fighting from an elevated position gives a small Attack and Defense bonus against lower opponents, but mounted characters already include height in their mounted bonus unless charging down a steep slope.
quotes: he enjoys an advantage that often translates to a +1 bonus to Attack and Defense in both melee and missile combat against opponents lower than himself

entries.title: Light Sources and Range of Visibility
entries.summary: Table giving the longest range at which each level of concealment applies in conditions such as moonlight, torchlight, rain and fog, with an optional Perception roll to reduce the concealment by a step.
quotes: a Perception roll of 9+ can sometimes reduce (by one step) the level of concealment due to poor visibility

entries.title: Fighting Indoors and in Narrow Spaces
entries.summary: Limits how many opponents can attack a defender in confined spaces such as against a wall or in a corridor, and notes cover, concealment and a penalty for large weapons in cramped quarters.
quotes: A character with his back to a wall can be attacked only by four opponents at once.

entries.title: Magical Devices in Warfare
entries.summary: Practical limits on using enchanted devices in battle: high-level effects are costly, carrying and activating items mid-fight is dangerous, a Group target needs a clearly separated group so crowds rarely qualify, and Aegis-protected covenants are immune to breaching devices.
quotes: a group must be clearly separated from others of its kind (ArM5, page 113)
devices like the Instant Breach are useless against covenants protected by an Aegis of the Hearth

entries.title: Travel
entries.summary: Guidelines for daily travel distances on foot, mounted, by cart and at sea, and the Long-Term Fatigue cost of hurried travel.
quotes: Attempts to travel quickly cost one Long-Term Fatigue level per day, as long as the characters actually travel.

entries.title: Ship Combat
entries.summary: Overview of how ships fight: boarding and cramped melee are usual, with artillery, ramming and oar-shearing as alternatives.

entries.title: Softening the Enemy (artillery, ramming, shearing oars)
entries.summary: Rules for shipboard artillery kills, galley ramming resolved by opposed captain rolls, and shearing oars to incapacitate rowers.
quotes: Two captains compare rolls of (stress die + Intelligence + Profession + up to 3 for experienced crews)

entries.title: Boarding and Melee
entries.summary: Captains' opposed rolls decide whether a predator boards or a victim escapes, followed by group combat with a height bonus for merchant ships and extra crew from sacrificed cargo space.
quotes: the two captains compare rolls of (stress die + Intelligence + Profession + up to 3 for experienced crews)
The added height grants them a +3 bonus on Attack and Defense Totals until they are boarded.

entries.title: Sea Monsters (attacks on ships)
entries.summary: How creatures of different Size threaten a ship: small ones barely harm it, while large ones hit automatically and destroy it as an environmental effect over rounds chosen by the storyguide.
quotes: Ships are so large that melee attacks against them automatically hit, and missile weapons have a +6 attack bonus.

entries.title: Guides and Messengers
entries.summary: Grogs plan journeys by itinerary and local knowledge, use Area Lore for navigation, and a successful Area Lore roll when planning a long journey can cut the travel time.
quotes: The Area Lore Ability is used for all sorts of navigation rolls
Intelligence + Area Lore roll of Ease Factor 12

entries.title: Travel Speeds
entries.summary: How far characters travel in a day on foot, horseback, by cart, coach or ship, including forced marches that cost Long-Term Fatigue, the effect of Athletics and Ride, changing horses, and how encumbrance and cross-country travel reduce distance.
quotes: 15 + (2 x Athletics) on good roads
30 + (2 x Ride) on good roads

entries.title: Travel Fatigue
entries.summary: Table of typical miles per day by mode of transport, with and without taking Long-Term Fatigue.

entries.title: Purchasing Supplies for Travel
entries.summary: Where and when grogs can buy food while traveling, with example prices and a rule of thumb for what it costs to feed a grog for a day.
quotes: Broadly speaking, it costs a Mythic Penny to feed a grog for a day, if you are buying rather than growing his food.

entries.title: Arranging Accommodation
entries.summary: Finding lodging in remote places uses a Communication + Folk Ken roll against an Ease Factor set by the kind of accommodation, with The Gift's social penalty applying if the peasants have talked with the magi.
quotes: make a Communication + Folk Ken roll, using the Ease Factors in the following table

entries.title: Journeying Underwater
entries.summary: Covers the difficulties of moving, fighting, seeing, casting and descending underwater: slow swimming, weapons and trained groups that stop working, blurred vision, restricted spellcasting, and pressure that drains Fatigue levels with depth.
quotes: Characters who know how to swim will travel by swimming at half the speed that a typical person walks.
After each 10 paces of descent, a character loses one-tenth of his current depth minus soak (extra soak from armor does not apply), in fatigue levels.

related.text: ArM5 p.122 Lungs of the Fish

entries.title: Boats and boating (piloting, rowing and boat damage)
entries.summary: Basic rules for buying, crewing and piloting a small boat or rowing boat: Ability and Characteristic combinations for piloting, weather Ease Factors, quality and crew modifiers, fatigue from rowing, failure, botches and Damage levels.
quotes: The Ease Factor for any rolls depends on the weather: mild wind or rain requires an Ease Factor of 3, a squall requires an Ease Factor of 9, an average storm an Ease Factor of 12, and a tempest an Ease Factor of 15 or more.
Piloting rolls are made with Strength + Athletics
Fatigue checks must be made after every hour of rowing in calm seas, every half hour in choppy waters, and every quarter of an hour in stormy weather.

related.text: City & Guild p.77 Damage levels and Stress checks

entries.title: Schools of Magical Combat
entries.summary: Introduces the Flambeau idea of a 'school' of magical combat: a named, coherent style combining particular Arts, Abilities and spells.

entries.title: Choosing a School
entries.summary: How magi pick a combat school to suit their Hermetic Virtues and Flaws, and how Flambeau apprentices have a school chosen for them by their parens.

entries.title: Schools of Magical Combat at a Glance
entries.summary: Quick-reference table of the six example schools, what each does, and the Virtue recommended for it.
quotes: | The Founder | Attacks using fire | Puissant Ignem |

entries.title: The School of the Founder
entries.summary: Fire-based combat school: strengths, weaknesses and play advice for a magus who relies on Ignem attacks.
quotes: Ignem spells do excellent damage compared to other spells of similar magnitude.

related.text: ArM5 p.87 Spell Mastery magic resistance

entries.title: The School of Apromor
entries.summary: Perdo-based combat school aimed at damaging opponents directly, with versatile non-damaging uses but heavy demands on Penetration and Spell Mastery.
quotes: Perdo spells usually disregard the target's Soak

entries.title: The School of Boreas
entries.summary: Combat school built on the single combination of Perdo Ignem, using cold and darkness; a narrower, cheaper-to-learn alternative to the Apromor and Founder styles.
quotes: The School of Boreas relies on the single Form-Technique combination of Perdo Ignem.

entries.title: The School of Ramius
entries.summary: Combat school that bypasses Magic Resistance with mundane weapons backed by defensive magic, including the problem of a magus's own Parma Magica blocking self-targeted spells.
quotes: Spells of Personal Range always bypass the caster's own Magic Resistance (ArM5, page 85), but Touch- and Voice-Range spells are resisted.

entries.title: The Schools of Sebastian
entries.summary: A family of minor combat schools that conjure harmful substances with Forms other than Ignem, usually supported by a Magical Focus.
quotes: Most members of the Sebastian family of schools have a Magical Focus (either Major or Minor)

entries.title: Magical Foci for the Schools of Sebastian
entries.summary: Sample Magical Foci by Form suited to the Sebastian schools, with note on which count as Major.
quotes: Except where noted, all of them would count as Minor Magical Foci.

entries.title: The School of Vilano
entries.summary: Combat school based on indirect spells that bypass Magic Resistance; notes aiming with Finesse and the double botch risk of aimed spells.
quotes: indirect spells require two stress rolls (one to cast the spell and another to aim it) and therefore have two chances to botch.

entries.title: Indirect Spells from ArM5
entries.summary: List of core-book spells that can have at least partial effect without penetrating Magic Resistance, with notes on why each works.
quotes: Magic Resistance does not protect against non-magical stone falling due to gravity.

entries.title: The Tournament
entries.summary: Overview of how a tournament unfolds from the commencailles and regars through the estor, melee and prize feast.

entries.title: Rules of Melee
entries.summary: The customs of a tournament melee: safe territory, protection of non-participants, points of honor, and how knights break the rules.

entries.title: Ransom
entries.summary: How surrender and ransom work in a melee, what may reasonably be demanded from knights of different means, and the Reputation cost of failing to pay.
quotes: Those who do not make good their promises gain 1 experience point towards an appropriate negative Reputation.
Service cannot be demanded as a ransom, nor can oaths of loyalty.

entries.title: Companies of Men
entries.summary: Knights fight in companies acting as trained groups, who may try to isolate a target and grapple the rider to lead him off for ransom.
quotes: Companies engage as trained groups of usually no more than ten individuals (or six if using the core combat rules)
A grappled rider loses control of his horse to his attackers.

entries.title: Tournament Combat
entries.summary: Melee fighting uses the optional non-lethal combat rules, which characters may drop round by round, and special maneuvers from the optional combat chapter may be used.
quotes: Botches in non-lethal combat almost always inflict real damage to one party or another.

related.text: LoM Chapter Nine: Optional Combat Rules, Option: Non-Lethal Combat

entries.title: Jousting
entries.summary: How a joust is resolved: each charge is one combat round using the optional shock of the charge rules, with botches possibly breaking equipment or injuring horse or rider.
quotes: Each charge comprises a single combat round

related.text: LoM Chapter Nine: Optional Combat Rules, Option: Shock of the Charge

entries.title: Melee Events Table
entries.summary: A random-encounter table for the tournament melee, rolled with Prudhomme Reputation as a modifier, that says what kind of opponent presents itself and carries growing botch dice for each event rolled.
quotes: Rolls on this table have a modifier equal to the character's Prudhomme Reputation.
Botch dice on the roll are equal to 1 + (1 per melee event rolled so far).

entries.title: The Grand Charge
entries.summary: The first of two ways to play the tournament melee: a series of stress rolls on the Melee Events Table giving chances to claim ransom, with opponents accumulating wounds as the melee goes on.
quotes: characters in the melee make a stress roll on the Melee Events Table.
assume that the opponent(s) have picked up a new short-term light wound

entries.title: Tournament Prizes
entries.summary: Guidance on the kinds of prizes a tournament host offers, with vis as the simplest.
quotes: a rook (ten pawns) is a moderate prize

entries.title: Wolf pack hunt: overview of the five phases
entries.summary: Introduces the structured procedure a storyguide uses when a wolf pack hunts the characters: stalk, encounter, rush, chase and kill.
quotes: A wolf hunt has five main phases: the stalk, the encounter, the rush, the chase, and the kill.

entries.title: Pack hunt: the stalk
entries.summary: Tracking rolls to find and follow a trail, and the stealth-versus-awareness roll that determines how close a stalking pack creeps before the prey is alerted or spooked.
quotes: A Perception + Awareness roll is needed to find tracks, and a Perception + Hunt roll is needed to follow them.
The wolf pack should make a Dexterity + Stealth roll; the Ease Factor is the Perception + Awareness roll of the prey.
Each success made by the pursuers allows them to creep (10+Qik) paces closer to their prey.

entries.title: Pack hunt: the encounter
entries.summary: The point at which prey and predators confront each other: prey that holds its ground leads to the kill, prey that flees leads to the rush, and wolves try to isolate individuals from a group.
quotes: During the encounter wolves attempt to break up groups of prey, preferably isolating one or two from the rest.

entries.title: Pack hunt: the rush (short pursuit rules)
entries.summary: Round-by-round pursuit rules for a short sprint: opposed Quickness and Athletics rolls open or close the distance, running speeds differ for four-legged and two-legged creatures, and each round also risks a Fatigue level.
quotes: Rush Total: Quickness + Athletics – Encumbrance + stress die
Change of distance for winner (four legs): (10 + Quickness – Encumbrance) paces
Rush Fatigue roll: Stamina + Athletics – Encumbrance + stress die against Ease Factor 9

related.text: Lords of Men p.120 running speeds

entries.title: Pack hunt: the chase (long pursuit rules)
entries.summary: Long-distance pursuit rules: each round both sides test endurance for Long Term Fatigue, then compare a Pursuit Total against an Evasion Total, with modifiers for leg count and knowledge of the terrain, until one side wins enough rounds.
quotes: Chase Fatigue roll: Stamina + Athletics – Encumbrance roll against Ease Factor 12
Pursuit Total: Perception + Hunt – Fatigue penalty + Pursuit modifiers + stress die
Dexterity + Athletics – Fatigue penalty + Evasion modifiers + stress die

entries.title: Pack hunt: the kill (trained group and trip attacks)
entries.summary: How an attacking pack fights: a trained group led by the pack leader, swapping group members with a Leadership roll, and trip maneuvers that leave a target with a reduced Defense.
quotes: making a roll of Communication + Leadership + stress die against an Ease Factor of 9
If the Attack Total exceeds the Defense Total by three or more, then the target is tripped

entries.title: Sentry Duty (staying awake on watch)
entries.summary: Rules for grogs on watch: what they may and may not do, how Fatigue is handled, the Stamina + Concentration roll to stay awake, the Awareness penalty for sleeping sentries, and the penalty after being woken suddenly.
quotes: This involves a Stamina + Concentration roll; failure indicates that the character is dozing or asleep.
Stamina + Concentration + simple die
Characters who are asleep have a –9 penalty to any Awareness rolls.

entries.title: Double Duty
entries.summary: When trouble is expected, longer shifts are ordered and each grog makes a dusk Fatigue roll whose Ease Factor rises with each double-duty watch; failure costs a Long-Term Fatigue level, and none are regained until normal shifts or long uninterrupted sleep.
quotes: Stamina + simple die versus Ease Factor 3 + number of double duties

entries.title: Flogging
entries.summary: A public punishment with a strap that inflicts Light Wounds and Long-Term Fatigue losses depending on the number of blows.
quotes: 1, 2, or 3 Light Wounds are inflicted by this punishment

entries.title: Whipping
entries.summary: A harsher punishment of lashes with a long or short whip that inflicts Light, Medium or Heavy Wounds by number of lashes, with a limited recovery time before pay is docked.
quotes: 10 lashes inflicts a Light Wound, 30 lashes a Medium Wound, and 50 lashes a Heavy Wound.

entries.title: Deprivation
entries.summary: Characters deprived of food, water or air make repeated Stamina checks with rising Ease Factor, losing Fatigue levels and then suffering worsening wounds.
quotes: The Ease Factor for the check starts at 3, and increases by one for every time period that passes.

entries.title: Deprivation Table
entries.summary: Table of the time between checks for deprivation of air, water and food.

entries.title: Magically Created Food and Deprivation (Covenant Survival)
entries.summary: Covenants hiding from Fimbulwinter face attacks if the site is not concealed, and magically created food made without vis builds up a Deprivation debt of Long-Term Fatigue with escalating Stamina Ease Factors and a Living Conditions penalty.
quotes: Each successive month of magical food increases the Ease Factor by 9 with the loss of three Long-Term Fatigue levels.
anyone living in such an environment suffers a –2 Living Conditions modifier

entries.title: Hazards of the Desert
entries.summary: Adjusts the Deprivation rules for desert travel (faster water checks, extra sun damage) and gives a stress roll to escape dry quicksand, with notes on brigands, storms and jinn.
quotes: The Deprivation check time for lack of water is reduced in the deserts to 4 hours, while the sunlight does +1 non-combat damage if skin is left exposed
A character who is caught in an area of dry quicksand may make a Strength or Quickness stress roll against an Ease Factor of 9 in the first round

entries.title: Winter's Bite (Fimbulwinter exposure)
entries.summary: Sidebar describing how the Fimbulwinter grows harsher after a year or more of Aspects roaming, making Scotland and Scandinavia uninhabitable with Major Exposure hazard checks and driving migrations and travel difficulties.
quotes: Deprivation checks each hour, Ease Factor 9 or +3 frostbite damage

entries.title: Giants in Combat
entries.summary: Optional rules for fights between humans and giants: a defensive bonus for giants against scuffling, grappling and disarming, bending over, and the limits of Corpus spells on giants.
quotes: grant the giant a special defensive bonus equal to double the difference between its Size and a smaller opponent's
Giants of Size +4 or larger must bend over double in order to reach a Size 0 human with their hands.

entries.title: Optional Rule: Swarms
entries.summary: An optional rule for treating a mass of tiny creatures as one swarm that ignores defenders, can attack several targets each round, may resist ordinary weapons, and retreats and returns rather than being easily destroyed.
quotes: A swarm is a mass of creatures of Size –3 or smaller with a combined Size of +1 or more.
Swarms ignore defenders and can always reach their intended target.
Swarms may attack a number of targets equal to the swarm's size each round.

entries.title: Resolving Tomb Traps
entries.summary: An optional trap procedure in which each player frames a clever response and rolls only for it against a trap Ease Factor the storyguide adjusts per character, with actions resolved in Quickness order (endangered character first, trap last), Fast-Cast magic and Action Priority Rolls.
quotes: Each trap is assigned a base Ease Factor, indicating the complexity of its construction.
The actions are resolved in order of Quickness, but with the character actually in danger always being treated as fastest, and the trap always going last.

entries.title: Infant Character Design Notes (Wounds)
entries.summary: Warns that infant characters are extremely fragile and offers two options for damage: trading wounds for Flaws or adding the age modifier penalty to Wound Recovery rolls.
quotes: The second option is add the child character's age modifier penalty to any wound recovery roll that the character needs to make.

related.text: Lords of Men p.125 Option: Mitigating Deadly Wounds

entries.title: Locating a Zenodochium
entries.summary: Where zenodochia are found and how to roll to see whether a character knows of a nearby one, with different Ease Factors for residents and visitors and adjustments for Tremere and for rarity.
quotes: make an Intelligence + Order of Hermes Lore roll
In either case, Tremere characters have a +3 bonus to the roll.
Increase the Ease Factors by 3 if zenodochia are rare in your saga.

entries.title: Allies
entries.requires: An ally or agent from a Virtue or story event
entries.summary: A character with an ally or agent may claim that ally's forces, with the troupe's approval.
quotes: may claim the forces of that ally or agent, with the approval of the troupe.

entries.title: Affinity
entries.summary: A regional leader calls lesser nobles to his banner with a roll whose result multiplies his core vassal force, using the Allied Troops Table.
quotes: Presence + Leadership + Affinity score simple roll

entries.title: The Articles of War
entries.summary: The Church's Peace of God and Truce of God, which protect certain people and forbid fighting on certain days, and the sin of breaking them or executing prisoners.
quotes: The Truce of God (Treuga Dei) restricts the days on which war can be waged.

entries.title: Chevauchee
entries.summary: A scorched-earth raiding tactic, with a Living Conditions penalty to the Aging rolls of those who return to the ravaged land and a possible Infernal aura in extreme cases.
quotes: Those returning to such an area suffer a –2 Living Conditions modifier (in addition to any existing modifiers) to their next Aging roll.

related.text: Realms of Power: The Infernal pp.11, 15

entries.title: Allied Troops Table
entries.summary: Converts the result of the affinity roll into a proportion of extra allied forces, with a list of situational modifiers to the roll.
quotes: a character must roll better than 12 to raise additional allied forces past his own core force.

entries.title: Winning the Battle from Afar
entries.summary: When the player characters are not central to a battle, the storyguide simply decides its outcome from the needs of the wider story and the characters' actions.
quotes: the storyguide should simply decide the outcome of the battle

entries.title: Crusaders
entries.summary: How the Church raises an army to crusade, using the Senior Clergy character's Holy Influence roll against an Army Size Table.
quotes: is treated as having an affinity equal to the most prominent noble within his diocese or see

related.text: Realms of Power: The Divine pp.38, 93

entries.title: Knights Banneret and Mercenary Captains
entries.requires: Knight Banneret or Mercenary Captain status
entries.summary: These characters always treat their company as one combat group regardless of weight of numbers modifiers.
quotes: always treat their company as a single combat group regardless of any Weight of Numbers modifiers.

entries.title: Using Magic to Seize Advantage
entries.requires: Magic affecting terrain or troop deployment
entries.summary: Spells that alter terrain or misdirect troops add to the friendly Deployment Total.
quotes: Add the highest magnitude of any spell used to affect the terrain, or the deployment of troops, to the friendly side's Deployment Total.

entries.title: Mercenary Troops
entries.summary: Specialist mercenary troops may differ from the standard unit statistics, and a historical example of daily pay for knights, serjeants and infantry.
quotes: Richard's knights received one shilling per day while his mounted serjeants received four pence per day

entries.title: The Eastern Bastion
entries.summary: Notes on how magic fares against a massed army (foot soldiers exceed the base Individual size, weakening Group-target spells) and a summary of Mongol-style Magogoli battle tactics.
quotes: The footsoldiers are outside the range of a base Individual of Corpus, which also reduces the effectiveness of Target: Group spells fivefold.

entries.title: Warping of hedge wizards
entries.summary: Hedge wizards gain Warping Points by the usual methods except from living in a strong magic aura, and have no Wizard's Twilight; unGifted ones react like mundane characters and Gifted ones react in tradition-specific ways.
quotes: he does not accumulate Warping points due to living in a strong magic aura

entries.title: Elemental Warping
entries.summary: Elementalists gain elemental Personality Traits instead of Virtues and Flaws from Warping; the Traits add to Soak against the matching element, subtract from Recovery against matching humoral illness, and become Personality Flaws or madness as they rise.
quotes: divide the Form by 5 (rounded up), and add this result to the value of the corresponding Trait
You must subtract the value of the Trait from the character's Recovery rolls whenever he is suffering from an illness of the corresponding humor.
Treat Traits of +6 or more as Major Personality Flaws

entries.title: Elemental Traits
entries.summary: Describes the four elemental Personality Traits (Choleric, Melancholic, Phlegmatic, Sanguine), the Form and opposed Trait for each, and notes that opposed Traits never cancel out.
quotes: The effects of these Traits on the character's personality never cancel each other out

entries.title: Folk Witch Warping
entries.summary: Folk witches gain Warping Points as usual plus from botches, but not from Magic auras; each time the Warping Score rises she suffers the Witch Moon instead of Twilight.
quotes: She also gains Warping points when she botches using her Supernatural Abilities.

entries.title: The Witch Moon
entries.summary: The folk witch's equivalent of Wizard's Twilight: a month or more of lost Supernatural Abilities and a fever Medium Wound, with a monthly roll to end it and extra Warping Points on failure or botch.
quotes: TO END WITCH MOON: Stamina – Warping Score + stress die vs Ease Factor 6

entries.title: Effects of the Witch Moon
entries.summary: After recovering, the witch's experience is good or bad depending on whether the months taken exceeded her Warping Score, and the storyguide picks an effect from the matching list.
quotes: If the folk witch took more months to recover from the Witch Moon than her Warping score, then the experience is bad.

entries.title: Witch Moon: Good Experiences
entries.summary: Good Witch Moon outcomes: experience points in an existing Ability or Theory, a new Minor Virtue, or a new Supernatural Ability at score 1.
quotes: equal to 5 x number of months spent in the Witch Moon

entries.title: Witch Moon: Bad Experiences
entries.summary: Bad Witch Moon outcomes: lost experience in a Supernatural Ability or Theory per Warping Point gained, or a new Minor Flaw.
quotes: She loses 2 experience points in a Supernatural Ability or in Folk Witch Magic Theory for every Warping Point gained during the Witch Moon.

entries.title: Warping While Under Constant Magical Effects
entries.requires: Constant enchantments on people or places
entries.summary: Tables showing how many Warping Points and what Warping Score and effects accumulate over the years for targets under constant enchantments that improve living conditions.
quotes: The second table assumes a single level 40 enchantment producing five warping points per year.

entries.title: Appropriate Virtues and Flaws for Warped Buildings
entries.summary: Suggests the kinds of Virtues, Flaws, magical Qualities and Personal Powers a building may gain when it becomes warped.
quotes: a Personal Power (an effect of Personal Range OR constant duration of up to 25 levels)

entries.title: Cursewood: Trekking (stages, rolls and modifiers)
entries.summary: Procedure for crossing the Cursewood in five stages, each costing a Long Term Fatigue level, with a leader and guide, a terrain-dependent progress roll made with the guide's stats, and group-size and encumbrance modifiers.
quotes: The leader and guide can manage a group of people no larger than their combined Leadership scores; exceeding this causes additional hazards as shown later.
Each stage takes a number of hours to complete equal to the number of hazards suffered, although always at least one.
+1 per group member who knows the Ability used apart from the guide

entries.title: Cursewood: Trek Progress table
entries.summary: Converts the guide's progress roll into a number of hazards suffered in the stage, with extra hazards for oversized groups and a bonus or free stage for very high rolls.
quotes: Add one extra hazard for each person exceeding the maximum group size, defined as the combined Leadership scores of the leader and guide.

entries.title: Cursewood: Retreat and Defeat
entries.summary: A group that retreats suffers little harassment and needs no rolls, taking only an hour per stage, but the terrain resets so later visits are no easier.
quotes: they suffer minimal harassment on the way out, which takes only an hour per stage

entries.title: Cursewood: Rest, Sleep, and Supplies
entries.summary: Fatigue recovery in the woods: Long Term levels need a night's rest, Short Term recovery is slowed, hazards at night prevent recovery, supplies are spoiled and eating local plants or water wounds.
quotes: recovery times are doubled for Short Term Fatigue
ingesting any plants or water from the Cursewood immediately causes a Light Wound

entries.title: Cursewood: Hazards and Penetration
entries.summary: How hazards are chosen and when the spirit's effects must Penetrate, using Wyzwanie's Penetration with the regio bonus against characters weakened by the Infernal aura.
quotes: A hazard caused indirectly by Wyzwanie’s powers, like moving or reshaping terrain features, does not need to penetrate.
so gets a +7 bonus to Penetration

entries.title: Cursewood: Forest hazards
entries.summary: Sensory descriptions and example hazard events for forest stages, including corrupted trees, thorn walls and pitfalls with set damage.
quotes: A fall of 10 feet results in a +2 damage for mud, +5 for dirt, or +10 for rocks.

entries.title: Cursewood: Hill hazards
entries.summary: Example hazard events for hill stages, including loose-rock slides with Dexterity rolls and Ease Factors, hostile weather and exploding ground.
quotes: The Ease Factor is 6 to stay in place or 15 to move up the slope.

related.text: ArM5 p.125 Charge of the Angry Winds
ArM5 p.127 Talons of the Wind

entries.title: Cursewood: Swamp hazards
entries.summary: Example hazard events for swamp stages, including quicksand hands that lead to deprivation of air and churning waters needing a swim or boating roll, with botch consequences for progress.
quotes: Victims roll Strength + Swimming (or Profession: Boating) against an Ease Factor of 12 to reach the safety of the river banks.

related.text: ArM5 p.156 Hands of the Grasping Earth

entries.title: Cursewood: Using shortcuts and magic against the hazards
entries.summary: Guidance on how the spirit treats magical shortcuts and spellcasting: the regio can only be entered when led by the spirit, clever low-magnitude magic earns respect but invites a different hazard, and elemental specialists fare better though the hostile aura still risks fatigue and botches.
quotes: However the regio can only be entered by those led by Wyzwanie, and he only allows this once he is satisfied.

entries.title: The Falling of the World into Ruin (Moon Fragment Strikes)
entries.summary: A seasonal procedure for deciding when and how near moon fragments strike the player Tribunal, plus an Astronomy stress roll that lets a character foresee where the next strikes will land, with a penalty for each further season predicted.
quotes: Characters may make an Intelligence + Artes Liberales (Astronomy) Stress Roll.
The target Ease Factor is 12 in order to determine which area will be affected in the next season.

entries.title: Apocalypse Condition: Sickness
entries.summary: Smoke and ash cause non-natural sickness, raising the frequency of choleric diseases and imposing a modifier on aging rolls, even within covenants, which may in turn affect covenfolk loyalty.
quotes: These conditions that promote sickness also impose a –2 aging roll modifier.

entries.title: Apocalypse Condition: Lunacy
entries.summary: Manifest aether drives people mad according to their dominant humor, with the afflicted gathering into roaming discordant pilgrimages.
quotes: those with a dominant sanguine humor become hysterical

entries.title: Apocalypse Condition: Famine
entries.summary: Food becomes scarce, imposing a cumulative annual living standards modifier that covenants can offset with magical resources for their covenfolk and protected areas.
quotes: Each year after the first, a cumulative –1 living standards modifier is imposed as food becomes more scarce and less nutritious.

entries.title: Apocalypse Condition: Loss of Rule
entries.summary: Each season a mundane leader makes a Leadership stress roll to hold authority, with failures increasing a Poor Leader reputation and botches signalling an imminent uprising.
quotes: must make a Communication or Presence + Leadership stress roll against an Ease Factor of 9

entries.title: Apocalypse Condition: Aetheric Storms
entries.summary: Storms of aether sweep west across Europe, unbalancing humors and, at higher densities, causing damage per Diameter of exposure, with shelter giving protection.
quotes: Those caught in such storms suffer +8 damage each diameter that they are exposed.
Aetheric earth moves at 100 paces per round

entries.title: Example Traps and Trap Damage
entries.summary: A catalogue of mechanical traps with Build Costs and Ease Factors, including rules of thumb for rockfall, projectile and pit damage, head wires and poisoned powders.
quotes: For smaller rockfalls, a rule of thumb is +1 damage per 10 pounds of rocks.
calculate Damage as (Stress die + Weapon Damage Modifier from page 177 of the core rules)

entries.title: Means of Avoiding Traps
entries.summary: Traps take effect last in the combat round so characters can react, and slower traps such as flooding rooms give extended time to escape.
quotes: Traps, regardless of their type, impose their effects last in the combat round.

entries.title: Perception Checks and Trap Lighting
entries.summary: A Perception + Awareness roll lets a character notice a trap without triggering it, with Ease Factors modified by the quality of lighting.
quotes: Characters able to supply perfect lighting conditions (such as through a spell) decrease the Ease Factor by 3

entries.title: Evading Traps with Lords of Men Evasion
entries.requires: Optional Combat rules from Lords of Men
entries.summary: For troupes using the optional Lords of Men combat rules, a trap's Attack total is based on the trap setter's Intelligence and Profession and tested against the Evasion Combat Statistic.
quotes: assume the trap's Attack total is stress die + Intelligence of the trap setter + Profession of the trap setter

entries.title: Mongolian Bows
entries.summary: Describes Mongol double-recurve composite bows and horse bows and the specialized arrow types, with a key explaining the table markers for two-handed loading, combined bow and arrow modifiers, and non-lethal arrows.
quotes: two () indicate that you should add the values of the bow and arrow to determine the final modifier

entries.title: Mongolian Bow, Continued
entries.summary: Weapon table giving Initiative, Attack, Defense, Damage, range, Strength, Load and cost for the composite bow, horse bow and the special arrow types.

entries.title: Statistics for Guan Weapons
entries.summary: The adjustment applied to weapons made of stone or volcanic glass instead of metal, with the melee and missile weapon tables for the Guan.
quotes: Those Guan weapons constructed with stone or volcanic glass, in lieu of metal, and have a Damage modifier 2 points lower than usual, to a minimum Damage modifier of +1.

entries.title: Demons of Disease (Diseased Possession)
entries.summary: Infernal power by which a demon possesses a victim and spends Might to inflict a disease, with the victim getting a Disease Avoidance roll to expel it. Includes a worked example.
quotes: The demon must then spend one point of this Might per five points (or fraction) of the disease's Severity to inflict its victim with the contagion

related.text: Realms of Power: The Infernal pp.32-33 (Possession)

entries.title: Purifying Touch and Immunity
entries.summary: Clarifies which diseases the Lesser and Greater Purifying Touch Virtues can cure and what the Lesser and Greater Immunity Virtues protect against.
quotes: Any Minor or Serious disease can be chosen as the disease cured by this Virtue.

entries.title: Leprosy
entries.summary: Describes leprosy as an incurable Divine mark that cannot be cured except by Divine intervention, how communities treat lepers, and the game effects of the Leprosy Flaw on Living Condition, Aging Crises and reputation.
quotes: Lepers gain the Major General Flaw Leprosy.
Due to its Divine origins, leprosy cannot be cured except by Divine intervention

related.text: ArM5 p.133 Curse of the Leprous Flesh

entries.title: Claw and Fang
entries.summary: A table of weapon statistics for dragon claws and teeth, with large versions for dragons bigger than Size +2.
quotes: Dragons larger than Size +2 usually have large claws and/or large teeth.

entries.title: Constriction Attacks (Option)
entries.requires: Being type: Dragon, worm or large serpent
entries.summary: An optional rule for dragons and serpents to constrict smaller victims using the grappling rules, depriving them of air.
quotes: A dragon can only constrict a victim whose Size is less than its own.
a constriction attack has the following weapon statistics: Init 0, Atk +3, Dfn 0, Dam n/a
The victim must make a Stamina check every 30 seconds, that is, every five rounds, or suffer the normal effects of deprivation.

entries.title: Multiple Attacks by Multi-Headed Dragons
entries.summary: Sample magical dragon statistics whose bite footnote sets how many attacks a huge creature can make against a single target in one round, scaling with the target's Size.
quotes: he can only attack a specific Size 0 target twice in a single round
For each Size above 0, the dragon can add an additional attack to that target in the same round.

entries.title: Staging a Tournament
entries.summary: How often tournaments of different sizes occur and when in the year they are held.
quotes: a large tournament — in excess of a thousand knights — can be found on average once per season

entries.title: Bohorts, Tirocinia, and Jousts
entries.summary: Defines the informal bohort, the youth-only tirocinium and the joust as variants of the tournament, and points to the non-lethal combat rules for the bohort.
quotes: Use the non-lethal combat rules on ArM5, page 174

related.text: LoM Chapter Nine: Optional Combat Rules, Option: Non-Lethal Combat

entries.title: High Ambition
entries.requires: Characters wishing to influence the whole melee
entries.summary: Runs the melee as a massed combat with custom story events, applying a short list of modifications to the massed combat rules.
quotes: There is no territorial advantage or weight of numbers bonus.

entries.title: Environmental Temperatures
entries.requires: Flaw: Warped Senses (Sensitive to Cold / Sensitive to Heat)
entries.summary: Chart ranking environmental conditions from unnaturally hot to unnaturally cold, used to judge how far a character with temperature sensitivity is from the conditions it is accustomed to.
quotes: Comfortable for a normal inhabitant of the Normandy, Rhine, Stonehenge, and Hibernia Tribunals

entries.title: Hellfire Damage and Escaping a Burning Regio
entries.summary: Rules for passing through supernatural hellfire: damage per exposure, much larger damage for total immersion, a Soak bonus for magi from their Ignem Form, and ways to avoid immersion by flying, teleporting or wards. The fire is a natural feature of the regio so cannot be dispelled or blocked by Magic Resistance.
quotes: These terrifically hot black flames inflict +15 damage.
Any character running through the flames takes +60 damage (due to total immersion; ArM5, page 181).

entries.title: Bath: Effects of the Baths
entries.summary: Bathing at Bath gives bonuses to Disease Recovery rolls depending on the care received, and the storyguide may instead pick other effects such as suppressing Flaws, bonuses to Aging, wound recovery or study totals.
quotes: A character attempting Disease Recovery rolls adds +5 if given a full course of care, +3 if she bathes regularly and cares for herself, and +1 if she simply bathes each day until the symptoms abate.

related.text: Art and Academe p.46 and p.58 Disease Recovery

entries.title: Bath: A Fourth Set of Baths (Gift-suppressing baths and vis)
entries.summary: An optional hidden set of baths that suppresses the social penalties of The Gift for a time, allows a spent Confidence point to be regained once per story, and can yield Vim vis from the skin of Gifted bathers tied to their Warping Score.
quotes: The waters here suppress the negative communication effects of The Gift, for a week with each bathing.
The oil can only be drawn from a magus once after each time his Warping Score increases, and forms an Arcane Connection to the magus.

entries.title: The Fallen Star: Searing Light of Heaven
entries.requires: Encounter with the fallen star (End of Time chapter)
entries.summary: Statistics the blinding light of the fallen star as a Hermetic effect with no Penetration, with a Stamina stress roll to avoid blindness that magi can bolster with Ignem or Aether Form bonuses, and an explanation of the Spectacle Target.
quotes: Those affected must make a Stamina stress roll against an Ease Factor of 9 to avoid blindness.
(Effect: Base 5, +2 Sun, +4 Spectacle; Modifications: +1 for 2/day, +3 triggered at sunrise/set)

related.text: Houses of Hermes: Mystery Cults (Spectacle Target)

entries.title: Greek Fire
entries.summary: Rules for the Byzantine alchemical weapon: mass production with a workshop and lab text, botch dice per dose, and statistics and use of the hand-held siphon.
quotes: He can supervise a number of subordinates equal to his Leadership score.
One botch die is rolled for every dose being manufactured
Init –2, Attack +4, Defense 0, Damage +10, Range 5 paces, Minimum Strength +2, Load 3, Cost Expensive.
Each dose of Greek Fire is good for 10 sprays of the hand-held siphon.

entries.title: Trained Group Combat (Templars)
entries.summary: Templars who train together for a season count as a trained group in combat; without that season together they cannot form one.
quotes: who train together for a season are considered a trained group for the purpose of combat

entries.title: Loreley: Treacherous River Stretch
entries.summary: The narrowest stretch of the Rhine Gorge is dangerous to boats even without the siren, with a Boating roll needed by crews who have not learned the positions of the rocks, and the cliff has a Faerie aura.
quotes: Ease Factor 9 for those who have not learned the positions of the rocks

entries.title: Criamon and Twilight
entries.summary: Criamon magi are better at navigating Twilight, referring to the Twilight rules in the core book.

entries.title: Zenodochium Items and Warping
entries.summary: Explains that the high-power constant-effect items in a zenodochium give Warping to every human who rests there, and how long recovery from each wound severity takes.
quotes: any human character who remains within a zenodochium for a season accumulates 6 Warping Points
